surface_related_text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $(S,\Omega_-,\Omega_+,n)$ be a two-sided presentation of a compact embedded $C^2$ interface in $\Omega$ in the sense of [[def-em-surface-distribution]]: $\Omega\setminus S=\Omega_-\cup\Omega_+$ are the two open sides and $n:S\to\mathbb R^3$ is the continuous unit normal pointing from $\Omega_-$ to $\Omega_+$. Let $F:\Omega\setminus S\to\mathbb R^3$ be of class $C^1$ on $\Omega_-$ and on $\Omega_+$ separately, with one-sided $C^1$ traces on $S$: $F$ and each first partial derivative $\partial_iF$ extend continuously from each side to $S$, and the traces $F_+,F_-\in C^0(S;\mathbb R^3)$ give the jump $[F]=F_+-F_-$.

Let $\{\partial_iF_j\}$, $\{\operatorname{div}F\}$ and $\{\operatorname{curl}F\}$ denote the locally integrable fields equal on $\Omega_\pm$ to the corresponding classical derivative of $F$; these are regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]). Then, away from the edge $\partial S$ of the interface and in the distributional sense,

as distributions on the open set $\Omega\setminus\partial S$: for every test function $\psi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\psi\cap\partial S=\varnothing$ the pairings of both sides agree. Here $\delta_S$ is the surface distribution of [[def-em-surface-distribution]], $n\cdot[F]=\sum_i n_i[F_i]$, and $n\times[F]$ is the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. A moving interface with $\partial_tS\ne0$ requires additional terms and is not covered; the stationary jump formulas may not be reused for a moving interface. Nothing is asserted at the edge $\partial S$.

**Given:** The open set $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$; a two-sided compact embedded $C^2$ interface $S$ with sides $\Omega_\pm$ and unit normal $n$ from $\Omega_-$ to $\Omega_+$; a field $F$ of class $C^1$ on each side with one-sided $C^1$ traces; and a test function $\psi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\psi\cap\partial S=\varnothing$.

[F1] Surface distributions and jumps: $\delta_S(\varphi)=\int_S\varphi\,dS$, the density functional and the jump $[F]=F_+-F_-$ are those of [[def-em-surface-distribution]]; a field $C^1$ on each side with one-sided continuous traces has locally integrable components, and the traces extend continuously to $S$.

[F2] Distributional derivative and regular distributions: $\langle\partial_i u,\varphi\rangle=-\langle u,\partial_i\varphi\rangle$ for $u\in\mathcal D'(\Omega)$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]]), and a locally integrable function defines a distribution by integration ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[def-distribution]]).

[F5] Derivative conventions: divergence and curl are those of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]; the cross product satisfies $(u\times v)_k=\epsilon_{kij}u_iv_j$ in the right-handed convention of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], and the Euclidean inner product is that of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]; products and one-sided derivatives follow the usual product and chain rules ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).

1.1 By [F1] the components of $F$ and of its one-sided first derivatives are locally integrable on $\Omega$, the piecewise fields $\{\partial_iF_j\}$ are locally integrable, and $[F_j]$ is continuous on $S$; hence all the distributions displayed in the Statement are defined, and $n_i[F_j]\delta_S$ is the surface distribution of the continuous density $n_i[F_j]$ of [F1]. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Local computation: let $\varphi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ have support in a ball $B=B_k$ as in step 1.2. By [F2], $\langle\partial_iF_j,\varphi\rangle=-\int_{\Omega}F_j\partial_i\varphi=-\int_{\Omega_+}F_j\partial_i\varphi-\int_{\Omega_-}F_j\partial_i\varphi$. On each side apply the divergence theorem [F3] to the field $G^\pm:=F_j\varphi\,e_i$, which is $C^1$ on the closure of $\Omega_\pm\cap B$ with one-sided traces on the interface face and which vanishes identically near the faces lying in $\partial B$ because $\operatorname{supp}\varphi\subseteq B$; the outward normal of $\Omega_+$ on the interface face is $-n$ and that of $\Omega_-$ is $+n$, so $\int_{\Omega_+}\partial_i(F_j\varphi)=-\int_{S\cap B}(F_j)_+\varphi\,n_i\,dS$ and $\int_{\Omega_-}\partial_i(F_j\varphi)=\int_{S\cap B}(F_j)_-\varphi\,n_i\,dS$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and let $(S,\Omega_-,\Omega_+,n)$ be a two-sided presentation of a compact embedded $C^2$ interface in $\Omega$ in the sense of [[def-em-surface-distribution]]: $\Omega\setminus S=\Omega_-\cup\Omega_+$ are the two open sides and $n:S\to\mathbb R^3$ is the continuous unit normal pointing from $\Omega_-$ to $\Omega_+$. Let $F:\Omega\setminus S\to\mathbb R^3$ be of class $C^1$ on $\Omega_-$ and on $\Omega_+$ separately, with one-sided $C^1$ traces on $S$: $F$ and each first partial derivative $\partial_iF$ extend continuously from each side to $S$, and the traces $F_+,F_-\in C^0(S;\mathbb R^3)$ give the jump $[F]=F_+-F_-$.

Let $\{\partial_iF_j\}$, $\{\operatorname{div}F\}$ and $\{\operatorname{curl}F\}$ denote the locally integrable fields equal on $\Omega_\pm$ to the corresponding classical derivative of $F$; these are regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]). Then, away from the edge $\partial S$ of the interface and in the distributional sense,

$$\partial_iF_j=\{\partial_iF_j\}+n_i\,[F_j]\,\delta_S\qquad(i,j\in\{1,2,3\}),$$

and consequently

$$\operatorname{div}F=\{\operatorname{div}F\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\cdot[F]\,\delta_S,\qquad \operatorname{curl}F=\{\operatorname{curl}F\}_{\mathrm{piecewise}}+n\times[F]\,\delta_S,$$

as distributions on the open set $\Omega\setminus\partial S$: for every test function $\psi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\psi\cap\partial S=\varnothing$ the pairings of both sides agree. Here $\delta_S$ is the surface distribution of [[def-em-surface-distribution]], $n\cdot[F]=\sum_i n_i[F_i]$, and $n\times[F]$ is the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. surface_related_text: Adopt as a modelling postulate of this framework the following reduced circuit description, to be used only within its declared regime. Let the laboratory region, its chart and units and the compact smooth current class be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-si-conventions]] and [[def-em-steady-current-regime]], and let the material response be one of the branches of [[post-em-material-closure]].

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) as carried by the declared
distributional and surface source objects of [[def-em-weak-sources]]. In the
flat classical laboratory model of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the positive
constants and SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]], adopt the following
additional physical assumption for models using the declared point or
stationary-sheet sources: the locally integrable field pair and the
volume-plus-singular source pair of [[def-em-weak-sources]](a)-(d) must satisfy
its solution predicate (e). Explicitly,

(b) [Equilibrium and sources] the configuration is in the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] on the vacuum region: $B=0$, $J=0$, $E$ is the fixed-time electric field of [[def-em-fields]], the volume source density $\rho_v$ is a continuous real map on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ (C m$^{-3}$, [[def-em-sources]]) extended by zero to $D$; the **conductor charge is a stationary surface charge**, i.e. a continuous density $\sigma:\partial D\to\mathbb R$ (C m$^{-2}$) whose pairing with test functions is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) with tangential current $K=0$ and $S=\partial D$; and the field pair $(E,0)$ together with the source pair $(\rho_v+\sigma\,\delta_{\partial D},\ 0)$ satisfies the adopted distributional vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]]. Inside the conductor the field vanishes: $E\equiv0$ on $D$ (the **equilibrium condition**); equivalently the conductor interior is field-free and carries no volume charge.

(c) [Potential and equipotential convention] there is a function $\varphi\in C^0(\Omega)\cap C^2(\Omega_v)$ with $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\Omega_v$ and with $\varphi$ constant on each conductor body, $\varphi|_{D_j}\equiv V_j$ for real constants $V_j$ (volts, [[def-em-si-conventions]]); by continuity of $\varphi$ the trace of $\varphi$ on each $\partial D_j$ from the vacuum side equals $V_j$ as well. This is the single-function convention of an ideal conductor with no double layer: the model reads the same potential value on both sides of $\partial D_j$, while the normal component of $E$ may jump.

The mathematical content used to *name* the objects is exact and proved earlier on this page: the surface $\partial D$ of finitely many pairwise disjoint bounded $C^\infty$ bodies is a disjoint finite union of compact embedded smooth hypersurfaces, and in the bounded smooth ambient branch the vacuum region is again a bounded smooth domain whose boundary pieces are the outer boundary and the conductor surfaces. The stationary-sheet pairing $\sigma\,\delta_{\partial D}$ is the surface-distribution object of [[def-em-surface-distribution]] as used by [[def-em-weak-sources]](c), and the solution predicate for the field-source pair is the separately adopted [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]]; the postulate itself neither proves that predicate nor asserts that it is satisfiable for the declared data. The countable-choice convention belongs to those measure and distribution interfaces and is carried here explicitly ([[def-countable-choice]]).

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. In the named inertial laboratory model of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the positive constants and SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]], adopt the following additional classical physical idealization: a loop, infinite straight line or infinite cylindrical sheet source defined by [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1)-(c3), with zero charge density, is modeled by a time-independent $B$ satisfying exactly the admissibility predicate (c4), together with $E=0$ and $\rho=0$. Thus $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ hold distributionally on $\mathbb R^3$, with the stated off-source regularity, symmetry and decay; the electrostatic and temporal Maxwell identities are zero. This physical adoption extends to these explicitly declared source types only. It is separate from the earlier $L^1$-source and point/compact-sheet postulates, which do not include these line and noncompact sheet sources. No existence, uniqueness, finite self-energy, force product, self-force, apparatus accuracy, matter dynamics or empirical certainty is asserted.

This is an adopted physical assumption, not a theorem: it states which ideal models this framework elects to use, and it is not deduced from the vacuum equations or from any experiment. The mathematical content it refers to — the exact source functionals of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1)-(c3) and the admissibility predicate (c4) — is fixed by that definition; the postulate adds the physical decision to treat those declared objects as sources of fields in the named laboratory. Existence and distributional consistency of the fields for the line and sheet models are established separately by the mathematical lemmas of this page, and the physical reading of the compact thin-loop limit remains a declared idealization rather than a measured property of any coil. The assumption carries no empirical uncertainty record because it reports no measurement; any later empirical comparison must state its own preparation, apparatus and sampling assumptions, and agreement would support the model under those conditions rather than establish it.

(c) [Status and scope] This is an adopted extra temporal condition carrying the model's arrow-of-time content. It is not a theorem, not a consequence of the time-symmetric wave or Maxwell equations (which admit advanced and free solutions as mathematical objects), and not a deduction from experiment; it asserts no existence, uniqueness, regularity, support or decay for any source class, all of which must be supplied separately by theorems of this page. It selects a solution only of the models to which it is applied; it introduces no product of distributions, no source model, no self-force, no radiation reaction, no measured signal and no statistical claim. The retarded compact-source branch to which this selection applies is developed on this page as a conditional theorem, and the point-source branch is developed later on this page; neither existence statement is part of this postulate. For the separately declared point-source branch assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as in its exact source/field interfaces, and adopt the same no-free-addition retarded selection in the weak equations of [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], for the locally integrable field and proper point-current types of [[def-em-weak-sources]]. This extends the selection's model scope explicitly; neither existence nor an arbitrary convolution of noncompact distributions is postulated.

(c) [Maxwell-compatible sources] Suppose in addition that the field pair
$(E,B)$ represented by $A$ through the potential dictionary of clause (c) of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and the source fields $(\rho,J)$ satisfy the
smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell equations on $U$ (equivalently, by clause
(a) of [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]], the tensor system
$\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ together with the cyclic identity). Then
clause (a) of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] gives
$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ on $U$
([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), which in the chart reads
$\partial_\mu j^\mu=\partial_0(c\rho)+\operatorname{div}J=c^{-1}\partial_t(c\rho)+\operatorname{div}J=0$;
hence $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every compact gauge variation.

fields and $C^1$ sources satisfying the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell
equations, the continuity equation
$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ holds pointwise
([[pthm-em-charge-continuity]]).

Statement

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$,
[[def-countable-choice]]), inherited through the componentwise
fundamental-variation step of [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]] and
through [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]. Let
$U,N,A,j,F,S$ and the constants $c,\mu_0,\varepsilon_0$ be as in clauses (a)-(b)
of [[def-em-field-action-definition]]: $U$ bounded open with $\overline U$
compact in the laboratory chart image $cI\times\Omega$, $N$ an open
neighbourhood of $\overline U$, $A$ and $j$ smooth on $N$,
$F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$, $j=(c\rho,J)$ with the
source fields of [[def-em-sources]], and
$S[A]=c^{-1}\int_U\bigl[-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}+j^\nu A_\nu\bigr]d\lambda$.
For $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ write $\partial^\sharp\chi$ for the
vector field with contravariant components
$(\partial^\sharp\chi)^\mu:=\partial^\mu\chi=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\nu\chi$
([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]],
[[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). It is a compactly supported
smooth field variation. Thus $A^\mu\mapsto A^\mu+\partial^\mu\chi$ lowers to
$A_\nu\mapsto A_\nu+\partial_\nu\chi$; $A+\partial^\sharp\chi$ denotes this
vector addition.

(a) [Exact gauge difference, no boundary term] For every such $\chi$ one has
$F_{\mu\nu}(A+\partial^\sharp\chi)=F_{\mu\nu}(A)$ on $U$, because
$\partial_\mu\partial_\nu\chi-\partial_\nu\partial_\mu\chi=0$ for the smooth
$\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]); consequently the field term
of $S$ is unchanged and

$$S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]-S[A]=c^{-1}\int_Uj^\mu\,\partial_\mu\chi\,d\lambda=-c^{-1}\int_U(\partial_\mu j^\mu)\,\chi\,d\lambda,$$

the second equality being the distributional integration-by-parts identity for
the locally integrable fields $j^\mu$ and the smooth compactly supported
$\chi$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]],
[[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]],
[[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]); no
boundary term arises precisely because $\chi$ is compactly supported in $U$.

(b) [Equivalence for smooth sources] If $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ on $U$ (the
source is conserved), then $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every
$\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$. Conversely, if
$S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every such $\chi$, then
$\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ pointwise on $U$: the function $\partial_\mu j^\mu$ is
continuous on the open $U$ and pairs to zero against every compactly supported
smooth $\chi$, so [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]] applies. Hence for
smooth prescribed sources the invariance of the field action under all compact
gauge variations is equivalent to the conservation of the four-current.

(c) [Maxwell-compatible sources] Suppose in addition that the field pair
$(E,B)$ represented by $A$ through the potential dictionary of clause (c) of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and the source fields $(\rho,J)$ satisfy the
smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell equations on $U$ (equivalently, by clause
(a) of [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]], the tensor system
$\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ together with the cyclic identity). Then
clause (a) of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] gives
$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ on $U$
([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), which in the chart reads
$\partial_\mu j^\mu=\partial_0(c\rho)+\operatorname{div}J=c^{-1}\partial_t(c\rho)+\operatorname{div}J=0$;
hence $S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi]=S[A]$ for every compact gauge variation.

(d) [Distributional reading] If $j^\mu$ is a distribution on $U$
([[def-distribution]]), the gauge-difference pairing
$c^{-1}\langle j^\mu,\partial_\mu\chi\rangle$ is defined for every test
function $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ and equals
$-c^{-1}\langle\partial_\mu j^\mu,\chi\rangle$ by the signed definition of the
distributional derivative; hence the pairing vanishes for every compact gauge
variation if and only if $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ as a distribution. This is a
statement about the pairing only: the smooth $j$ of the definition is retained
whenever the functional $S$ itself is used, and no products of distributions
are formed.

Scope: the item computes the gauge variation of the field action and its
compatibility with source conservation; it does not derive the field equations
from gauge invariance, does not assert that conservation of a source implies
stationarity, does not treat global or topological obstructions, and uses no
Noether machinery.

$$\varphi_j|_{\partial D_k}=\delta_{jk},\qquad \varphi_j|_{\partial\Omega}=0,$$
so that $-\Delta\varphi_j=0$ on $\Omega_v$ with the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], and let $\nu$ be the outward normal of $\Omega_v$ (so on $\partial D_j$ the normal $\nu$ points into the conductor). Define the **capacitance matrix** by
$$C_{jk}:=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\frac{\partial\varphi_k}{\partial\nu}\,dS,\qquad j,k=1,\dots,m,$$
the flux integrals of continuous functions over the compact embedded hypersurfaces $\partial D_j$ (normal derivative of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]) ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]]). Then:

$$U(V)=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\Omega_v}|\nabla\varphi^V|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac12V^{T}CV=\frac12\sum_{j=1}^mV_jQ_j(V),$$

([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]],

equations

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$

hold in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$ with distributional derivatives. This

surface_related_text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) inherited from the surface and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(\Omega;D_1,\dots,D_m;\Omega_v;E;\rho_v;\sigma;V_j)$ be a model of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] with surface $S:=\partial D$ and vacuum region $\Omega_v$, with the fields of [[def-em-fields]], the constants and units of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] carried by the model, and suppose additionally that the field $E$ satisfies the joint one-sided $C^1$ regularity hypothesis of [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]] across $S$: around every $x_0\in S$ each side of $S$ is the restriction of a $C^1$ field on an open neighbourhood of the corresponding closed side of a smaller graph chart. Let $n$ denote the unit normal on $S$ pointing from the conductor side into the vacuum side (equivalently: $n$ is the inward normal of $\Omega_v$ and the outward normal of $D$ on $S$, by the local exterior conductor chart; in the bounded smooth ambient branch this is the sign convention of [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]](c)), and let $E_+$ denote the vacuum-side trace of $E$ (the field is zero on the conductor side, so $[E]=E_+$). Then, pointwise on $S$:

(b) [Normal derivative of the potential] with $\varphi$ the model's potential and $\partial\varphi/\partial n:=\nabla\varphi_+\cdot n$ the one-sided normal derivative in the direction $n$ from the conductor into the vacuum ([[def-classical-normal-derivative]]), one has

(c) [Equipotential boundary traces] the trace $\varphi_+$ of $\varphi$ on $S$ is constant on each connected component of $S$, with value $V_j$ on every connected component contained in $\partial D_j$; consequently the boundary value problem in the vacuum region is a Dirichlet problem whose data are the constants $V_j$ on the conductor surfaces.

(f) [Scope] The statement is pointwise and stationary: it assumes the one-sided joint regularity above, a $C^\infty$ conductor surface, and the pure electrostatic regime; it excludes moving surface charge, normal sheet currents, magnetic sheet sources, nonsmooth or cornered conductors, fields without one-sided traces, forces, energy and any measurement; no self-force or material response is asserted.

**Given:** A model of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] with conductor surface $S=\partial D=\partial D_1\cup\cdots\cup\partial D_m$, vacuum region $\Omega_v$, field $E$ with $E\equiv0$ on $D$, continuous stationary surface density $\sigma$ on $S$, potential $\varphi\in C^0(\Omega)\cap C^2(\Omega_v)$ with $E=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\Omega_v$ and $\varphi\equiv V_j$ on $D_j$, and the joint one-sided $C^1$ regularity of the statement across $S$.

[F1] The conductor model: $E\equiv0$ on $D$; the pair $(E,0)$ with the source pair $(\rho_v+\sigma\delta_S,0)$, $K=0$, satisfies the adopted distributional vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]]; $\sigma$ is the stationary-sheet source of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) under [[def-em-surface-distribution]]; $\varphi$ is continuous on $\Omega$ and $C^2$ on $\Omega_v$ with $E=-\nabla\varphi$ there, constant on each $D_j$ with value $V_j$ ([[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-si-conventions]]).

[F2] The fixed-vacuum-jump theorem: under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the stationary compact embedded $C^2$ interface hypotheses, the joint one-sided $C^1$ field regularity and the weak Maxwell equations with the stationary-sheet source of [F1], one has pointwise on $S$ $n\cdot[E]=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$, $n\times[E]=0$, $n\cdot[B]=0$, $n\times[B]=\mu_0K$, with $[F]=F_+-F_-$ and $n$ pointing from the $\Omega_-$ side to the $\Omega_+$ side ([[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]], [[def-em-surface-distribution]]).

[F3] For a bounded $C^\infty$ conductor surface the outward normal of the vacuum region on $\partial D_j$ is $n_j=-n$ (the negative of the conductor's outward normal) whenever the bounded smooth ambient hypothesis of [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]](c) is in force; the local exterior conductor chart of the model identifies the vacuum-side normal with the conductor's outward normal in general ([[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]](a), [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]](c)).

[F4] Classical one-sided normal derivative: for the vacuum side, $\partial\varphi/\partial n:=\nabla\varphi_+\cdot n$ is the normal derivative of the $C^1$ vacuum-side restriction $\varphi$ in the direction $n$, where $\varphi$ is $C^2$ on the vacuum side and its gradient has the continuous trace $-E_+$ ([[def-classical-normal-derivative]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).

1.1 By [F2] with the conductor side as $\Omega_-$ and the vacuum side as $\Omega_+$ (the normal $n$ of the statement points from the conductor into the vacuum, matching [F2]), the jump identities $n\cdot[E]=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and $n\times[E]=0$ hold pointwise on $S$; the conductor-side trace vanishes because $E\equiv0$ on $D$ [F1], so $[E]=E_+-0=E_+$. This gives $n\cdot E_+=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and $\sigma=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot E_+$, and $n\times E_+=0$, which is (a); if $\sigma=0$ at a point then $n\cdot E_+=0$ and $n\times E_+=0$ there, so $E_+=0$ by [F8], and the sign of $\sigma$ is the sign of $n\cdot E_+$ since $\varepsilon_0>0$. [F1, F2, F8, given]

2.2 Tangential constancy of the trace. Let $X:B\to S$ be one of the regular graph charts of $S$ (a compact embedded smooth hypersurface [F7]), and for $y\in B$ and small $s>0$ put $x_s:=X(y)+sn(y)$, a point of the vacuum side because $n$ points from the conductor into the vacuum. For fixed $s>0$ small the function $f_s(y):=\varphi(x_s)$ is $C^1$ with $\partial_if_s(y)=\nabla\varphi(x_s)\cdot(\partial_iX(y)+s\,\partial_i n(y))$, and $x_s\to X(y)$, $\nabla\varphi(x_s)\to-E_+(X(y))$ as $s\downarrow0$ because the vacuum-side field has the continuous trace $E_+$ and the chart is smooth [F4]; on each compact coordinate segment the $\partial_if_s$ therefore converge uniformly to $-E_+(X(y))\cdot\partial_iX(y)=0$, since $E_+$ is orthogonal to the tangent vector $\partial_iX(y)$ by $n\times E_+=0$ [step 1.1]; the functions $f_s$ converge to the continuous trace $\varphi_+\circ X$ because $\varphi$ is continuous on $\Omega$ [F1]. Hence $f'=0$ on $B$ by [F5], so $\varphi_+\circ X$ is constant on the connected parameter ball [F6]. As the finitely many graph patches of $S$ cover $S$ and overlap in connected pieces, $\varphi_+$ is locally constant on $S$, hence constant on each connected component of $S$ [F6]. On a component contained in $\partial D_j$ the value is $V_j$, because $\varphi$ is continuous on $\Omega$, equals $V_j$ on $D_j$, and the component of $S$ lies in the closure of $D_j$ [F1]. This is (c). [F1, F4, F5, F6, F7, step 1.1]

4.1 Data reading and scope. Clause (e) follows from the definitions in (d): the total charges are determined by the equilibrium solution through the displayed identities, while charge data enter only through a separate equilibrium problem, for which this theorem proves neither existence nor uniqueness [given]. The statement is pointwise on $S$ and stationary: no moving charge, normal sheet current, magnetic sheet source, corner or field without one-sided traces is considered, no product of distributions and no corner equation is formed, and no force, energy, radiation, self-force, material response or measurement is asserted [F1, F2]; the surface integrals exist but no regularity of a general ambient outer boundary is claimed [F7]. [F1, F2, F7, given, step 3.1] ∎

$$\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial n}=-\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \sigma=-\varepsilon_0\,\frac{\partial\varphi}{\partial n}.$$

(a) [Smooth compact sources] Let $\rho:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^1$ with compact support contained in $\overline B_R$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-metric-ball]]), put $\varphi:=\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho$ and $E:=-\nabla\varphi$.
Then $\varphi\in C^2(\mathbb R^3)$ ([[thm-newtonian-potential-for-holder-data-is-classical]]), and pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$

Moreover, with $Q:=\int\rho\,d\lambda_3$, for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ the absolutely convergent Coulomb integral representation holds, and its far-field bound holds for $|x|>2R$,
$$E(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{x-y}{|x-y|^3}\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)\quad(x\in\mathbb R^3),\qquad |E(x)|\le\frac{\| \rho\|_1}{\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^2}\quad(|x|>2R),$$
and for $|x|>\max(2R,1)$ the potential obeys the decay bound $|\varphi(x)|\le\bigl(|Q|/(4\pi)+R\|\rho\|_1/\pi\bigr)/(\varepsilon_0|x|)$ ([[lem-em-newtonian-far-field-gradient]], [[thm-decay-of-the-newtonian-potential-of-compactly-supported-data]]).
The pair $(E,0,\rho,0)$ therefore realises the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with source $\rho$, and $E$ is the field of the localised Newtonian potential.

$$-\Delta T_{\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho}=T_{\rho/\varepsilon_0}\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$$

([[thm-minus-laplacian-of-the-fundamental-solution-is-dirac]] for the first identity, [[lem-em-distributional-gradient-smooth-off-a-point]] for the passage from the potential to the field, [[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]).

Statement

Adopt the causal selection [[post-em-radiation-selection]]: these retarded fields are the fields of the source model (the compact smooth instance established by [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]). Define the **time-dependent electric dipole moment**

$$p(u):=\int_{B_a}y\,\rho(y,u)\,dy\in\mathbb R^3$$

(componentwise, about the fixed chart origin of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; it is the fixed-time analogue of the static source moment of [[def-em-electric-moments]]), and, as in the asymptotic theorem, $I(n,u):=\int_{B_a}J(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$, $V(n,u):=\partial_uI(n,u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$ and

$$D(u):=\frac{a}{c}\int_{B_a}\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|\,dy.$$

(a) [Moment identities] $p\in C^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^3)$, $p'(u)=\int_{B_a}J(y,u)\,dy$, $p''(u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u)\,dy$, $\int_{B_a}\rho_t(y,u)\,dy=0$ and the total charge $\int_{B_a}\rho(y,u)\,dy$ vanishes for every $u$.

(c) [Leading fields] With $\Gamma_E$, $\Gamma_B$ the constants of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]](b) (depending only on $a,c,\mu_0$ and the listed source suprema), for every $n\in S^2$, $u\in[t_0,T]$, $r\ge2a$:

$$\Bigl|E\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p''(u))\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0D(u)}{4\pi r},\qquad \Bigl|B\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{n\times E(rn,u+\tfrac rc)}{c}\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_B+\Gamma_E/c}{r^2}.$$

$$|R(u)|\le\frac{\mu_0\bigl(2|p''(u)|D(u)+D(u)^2\bigr)}{4\pi c},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)d\sigma=\frac{\mu_0}{6\pi c}|p''(u)|^2\ \text{ whenever } D(u)=0.$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited Lebesgue, spherical-harmonic and Newtonian interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). For every $l,m$ define the **spherical multipole moment of degree $l$**

$$q_{lm}:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^l\,Y_{lm}(y/|y|)\,\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y),$$

absolutely convergent because $|Y_{lm}|\le((2l+1)/(4\pi))^{1/2}$ on $S^2$ by the addition theorem and $|y|\le a$ $\lambda_3$-a.e. on the support, so the integrand is dominated by $a^l((2l+1)/(4\pi))^{1/2}|\rho|$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]). In every coefficient integral the factor $|y|^lY_{lm}(y/|y|)$ is defined at $y=0$ by its homogeneous polynomial extension: zero for $l\ge1$ and the constant degree-zero harmonic for $l=0$; this is a finite assignment at a null singleton and changes no integral. Write $x=rn$ with $r=|x|$ and $n\in S^2$. Then:

(a) [Exterior spherical multipole expansion] for every $x$ with $r>a$,

$$\varphi(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_{l=0}^{\infty}\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\,\frac{Y_{lm}(n)}{r^{l+1}}\,q_{lm},$$

the series converging absolutely and uniformly on $\{|x|\ge r_0\}$ for every $r_0>a$, with the tail after degree $N$ bounded by

$$\Bigl\|\,\varphi-\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_{l=0}^{N}\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\frac{Y_{lm}(n)}{r^{l+1}}q_{lm}\Bigr\|_{\infty,\{|x|\ge r_0\}}\le\frac{\|\rho\|_1\,a^{N+1}}{4\pi\varepsilon_0\,r_0^{N+2}\,(1-a/r_0)};$$

$$\frac{1}{8\pi\varepsilon_0r^3}\,n_iQ_{ij}n_j;$$

(c) [Regularity and termwise differentiation] $\varphi$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\{|x|>a\}$, the series in (a) may be differentiated termwise to every order, the differentiated series converging uniformly on every compact subset of $\{|x|>a\}$; in particular the field $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ of [[def-em-fields]] equals $-\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\sum_{l,m}\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\nabla_x\bigl(Y_{lm}(n)r^{-l-1}\bigr)q_{lm}$ on $\{|x|>a\}$, with the same uniform convergence on compact subsets;

$$\varphi_f(rn)=\sum_{l=0}^\infty\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}(r/R)^lf_{lm}Y_{lm}(n),$$

with the constant degree-zero value at $r=0$. claim:
Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the cited solvability theorem ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega_v\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain in the sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] with finitely many connected components (the vacuum region of the additional bounded $C^\infty$ ambient branch of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] by [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]], or any bounded smooth domain), let $\rho$ be smooth on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ (fixed-time volume source density, C m$^{-3}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]) and let $\varepsilon_0>0$ be the framework constant. Then the electrostatic boundary value problems on $\Omega_v$ are solvable in the following exact senses, and the solutions are the fields of the pure electrostatic regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with volume source $\rho$:

(a) [Dirichlet branch] for every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega_v)$ there is exactly one $\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ with

$$-\Delta\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0\quad\text{on }\Omega_v,\qquad \varphi|_{\partial\Omega_v}=g,$$

with $\Delta$ the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]];
and it is the unique weak $H^1$ solution with trace $g$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] for the class); the field $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ ([[def-em-fields]]) is $C^\infty$ on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ and $(E,0)$ realises the pure electrostatic regime with source $\rho$ on the vacuum region.

(b) [Neumann branch] for every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega_v)$ with

$$\int_{\Omega_v^{(j)}}\rho\,dx+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial\Omega_v^{(j)}}g\,dS=0\qquad\text{for every connected component }\Omega_v^{(j)}\text{ of }\Omega_v,$$

there is $\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ with $-\Delta\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and $\partial_\nu\varphi=g$ (outward normal $\nu$, [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]), unique up to one additive constant per connected component; the normalisation $\int_{\Omega_v^{(j)}}\varphi\,dx=0$ for every $j$ selects exactly one. The compatibility is also necessary in the sense of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](b).

(c) [Conductor reading and surface-charge realization] for the separated compact-body conductor geometry and zero-interior-volume convention of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], additionally assuming $\Omega$ is a bounded $C^\infty$ ambient domain, with outer boundary data $g_0\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ on $\partial\Omega$ and constants $V_j$ on the conductor surfaces $\partial D_j$ (constant functions are smooth on the compact disjoint boundary pieces), the combined datum is a special case of (a); the field $E:=-\nabla\varphi$ on $\Omega_v$ extended by $E:=0$ on the conductor satisfies the adopted distributional vacuum Maxwell equations [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]] with the source pair $(\rho_v+\sigma\,\delta_{\partial D},\,0)$, where $\sigma:=\varepsilon_0\,n\cdot E_+\in C^\infty(\partial D)$ is the constructed continuous surface-charge density, agreeing afterwards with [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]] ([[def-em-weak-sources]](c), [[def-em-surface-distribution]], [[lem-em-interface-derivatives]]); the total charges $Q_j=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}n\cdot E_+\,dS$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]) are thereby determined by the data, and $\varphi$ is constant on each $\partial D_j$ with value $V_j$.

(d) [Stationary sheet charge in the vacuum region] for finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces $\Gamma$ strictly inside $\Omega_v$, a smooth sheet density $\sigma_\Gamma$ on them, and outer Dirichlet data $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega_v)$, there is a weak solution $\varphi\in H^1(\Omega_v)$ which is $C^\infty$ on the closure of each side of every $\Gamma$, unique by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](c)(iii), solving the weak equation with right-hand side $\int_{\Omega_v}\rho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma_\Gamma\,Tv$; its flux jump is $n\cdot[\varepsilon_0\nabla\varphi]=-\sigma_\Gamma$, equivalently $n\cdot[E]=\sigma_\Gamma/\varepsilon_0$ in the sign convention of [[pthm-em-fixed-vacuum-jumps]]. This is the vacuum ($\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0$) transmission branch; no dielectric coefficient is introduced.

(e) [Scope] all existence statements are the ones proved in [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] for its stated smooth bounded domains, smooth uniformly positive coefficients (here $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0 I$), smooth data and finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces; the coefficient is the smooth positive constant $\varepsilon_0I$ on every side in the transmission clause. Excluded: nonsmooth boundaries, corners, edges, coefficient loss of regularity, prescribed total charges for conductor bodies (the free equipotential problem), unbounded exterior regions without a stated decay class, dielectric material response (belonging to the material-response page) and any measurement, apparatus or empirical claim. The theorem asserts existence of the potential, not of a physical equilibrium; the ideal conductor is the adopted model of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]].

surface_related_text: Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the cited weak-solvability and trace suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega_v\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain with finitely many connected components (the vacuum region of the additional bounded $C^\infty$ ambient branch of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] by [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]], or any bounded smooth domain), let $\rho$ be continuous on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ (the fixed-time volume source density, C m$^{-3}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]), and let $\varphi_1,\varphi_2\in C^2(\overline{\Omega_v})$ be real potentials of the pure electrostatic regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with fields $E_i:=-\nabla\varphi_i$ of [[def-em-fields]] and

(c) [Weak variants] (i) if $g\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega_v)$ ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]) is prescribed as a trace and $\varphi_1,\varphi_2\in H^1(\Omega_v)$ are weak solutions of the Dirichlet problem with the same trace $g$, then $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$; (ii) if the conormal data are prescribed compatibly, weak $H^1$ solutions are unique modulo constants on each connected component, and for connected $\Omega_v$ this is the normalised solution of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]; (iii) [sheet/transmission variant] for the finite disjoint smooth interfaces and outer Dirichlet data of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](c), the globally $H^1$ solution is unique, and for compatible outer Neumann data it is unique modulo componentwise constants until the componentwise means are fixed.

(d) [Physics reading and conductor case] on a star-shaped vacuum domain the curl-free $C^1$ field has an interior $C^2$ potential by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-potential]]. This alone does not supply closure regularity, $H^1$ membership, a trace, or prescribed boundary data; each application of (a)-(c) additionally requires its stated regularity and identical boundary/source data. In the bounded conductor model, prescribed absolute conductor potentials $V_j$ and absolute outer Dirichlet data determine the potential and field uniquely in the admitted classical or weak class. Grounding fixes the additive constant exactly. If only relative potential differences are prescribed and the outer/reference data are also allowed to shift by the same constant, the common gauge constant is free; merely omitting outer boundary data does not establish field uniqueness.

(e) [Scope] uniqueness is conditional on the stated boundary or decay data: on an unbounded exterior region without a decay condition uniqueness fails: on $\Omega_R=\{x:|x|>R\}$ the functions $0$ and $u(x)=1-R/|x|$ are two distinct bounded harmonic functions with the same zero boundary trace and different limits at infinity, so the boundary, decay and regularity hypotheses above cannot be dropped. No existence is inferred from uniqueness; the classical branch requires $C^2$ up to the closure, the weak branches carry their own domain, coefficient and trace hypotheses, and no dielectric material coefficient or empirical claim is included. For the admitted conductor class with connected vacuum, fixed absolute conductor potentials and identical outer Neumann data also give exact uniqueness: this is a mixed boundary problem with a nonempty Dirichlet part, so there is no surviving additive constant. Existence for those mixed data is not asserted here. In that weak mixed branch, write $\mathcal V_D=\{v\in H^1(\Omega_v):Tv=0\text{ on }\partial D\}$. The compared potentials have the same prescribed conductor trace and satisfy $\varepsilon_0\int_{\Omega_v}\nabla v\cdot\nabla\varphi=\int_{\Omega_v}\rho v+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ for every $v\in\mathcal V_D$, with the same smooth outer normal datum $g$.

[F4] Weak Dirichlet uniqueness with prescribed trace: for a bounded $C^1$ domain and prescribed $g\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ there is exactly one $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $g$ solving the weak Dirichlet problem; in particular two weak solutions with the same trace and data coincide ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]], [[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]).

[F7] On a star-shaped open set a curl-free $C^1$ field $-E$ has an interior $C^2$ potential $\varphi$ with $\nabla\varphi=-E$ and $-\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}E$; no boundary regularity or normalisation at infinity is supplied ([[pthm-em-electrostatic-potential]]).

[F10] AC and AC$_\omega$ are declared mathematical assumptions of the cited weak-solvability, trace and measure suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]); $\varepsilon_0>0$ and $\Omega_v$, $\rho$, $\varphi_i$, $E_i$ are the objects of [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] and [[def-em-fields]]; the conductor model supplies the bounded smooth ambient branch and its connectedness requirement ([[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]]), and the mean-zero coercivity inequality is available on each connected bounded component ([[lem-em-mean-zero-coercivity-on-a-c-one-domain]], [[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]).

1.3 Weak variants. Clause (c)(i) is the uniqueness content of [F4]: two weak $H^1$ Dirichlet solutions with the same prescribed trace and the same right-hand side coincide. 1.4 Physics reading. On a star-shaped vacuum domain, [F7] supplies an interior $C^2$ potential for a curl-free $C^1$ field and nothing more: closure regularity, $H^1$ membership, a trace and boundary data are additional hypotheses, exactly as assumed in (a)-(c). For the bounded conductor model with its connected vacuum region [F10], fixed absolute conductor potentials and identical outer Dirichlet data are the Dirichlet data of (a) or (c)(i), so the difference of two admitted solutions has zero boundary data and is zero by the same uniqueness clause; grounding fixes the additive constant, while shifting both a relative-potential datum and every reference datum by a common constant leaves the difference of two solutions with the same data and hence with the same (fixed) uniqueness conclusion only for identical data — omitting outer data supplies no field uniqueness. This is (d). [F7, F10, given]

2.2 Mixed conductor data. Suppose the vacuum region is connected, $m\ge1$, $w$ is the difference of two admitted classical solutions with equal absolute conductor potentials and equal outer Neumann data. Then $w$ is harmonic, $w=0$ on the nonempty conductor boundary $\partial D$ and $\partial_
u w=0$ on the outer boundary $\partial\Omega$. Green's first identity [F9] gives $\int_{\Omega_v}|
abla w|^2=\int_{\partial\Omega_v}w\,\partial_
u w\,dS$, and each boundary piece carries one zero factor, so the integral vanishes; by [F9], $
abla w=0$ almost everywhere, and since $
abla w$ is continuous on the connected open $\Omega_v$ it vanishes everywhere, so $w$ is constant by the vanishing-differential characterisation; its zero conductor trace forces the constant to be $0$. In the weak mixed branch, the difference of two admitted solutions has zero conductor trace, so it is an admissible test in the homogeneous difference equation and the same zero-energy argument applies, with the mean-zero coercivity inequality of [F10] converting $
abla w=0$ into $w=w_{\Omega_v}$ as an $H^1$ class whose constant trace on the nonempty conductor boundary is zero. This sharpens (d); existence for mixed data remains unasserted. [F9, F10, given, step 1.4]

3.1 The unbounded witness and scope. On $\Omega_R=\{x:|x|>R\}$ put $u(x):=1-R/|x|$, and $u=0$, $\varphi\equiv0$. Then $u\in C^\infty(\Omega_R)$; since $R/|x|=4\pi R\,\Phi(x)$ is a constant multiple of the $n=3$ fundamental solution, it is harmonic off the origin [F8], and the constant $1$ has zero Laplacian, so $\Delta u=0$; moreover $u=0$ on $|x|=R$, $0<u<1$ on $\Omega_R$ and $u(x)\to1$ as $|x|\to\infty$. Thus $0$ and $u$ are two distinct bounded harmonic functions with the same zero boundary trace and different limits at infinity, witnessing that the boundary and decay hypotheses of (a)-(c) cannot be dropped. No existence statement is inferred from uniqueness anywhere above; the classical branch requires $C^2$ up to the closure, the weak branches carry their own domain, coefficient and trace hypotheses, and no dielectric coefficient, empirical value or measurement is included. This is (e). [F8, given] ∎

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the Lebesgue, polar and surface interfaces cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]).
Let $\rho\in C^1_c(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ with support in $\overline B_R$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-metric-ball]]), let $\varphi=\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho$ and $E=-\nabla\varphi$ be the smooth-branch Coulomb solution of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](a) with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]], and let $\Phi$ be the $n=3$ kernel, $\Phi(z)=1/(4\pi|z|)$ ([[def-laplace-fundamental-solution-with-positive-minus-laplacian-sign]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]).
Then:

(b) [Identity] they are equal:
$$\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho\varphi\,d\lambda_3=\frac{1}{2\varepsilon_0}\iint_{\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3}\Phi(x-y)\rho(x)\rho(y)\,d(\lambda_3\times\lambda_3)(x,y).$$
The last expression is the **external assembly work** of the ideal quasistatic bookkeeping family $\rho_s=s\rho$, $\varphi_s=s\varphi$ for $0\le s\le1$. An added test charge brought from infinity, where the potential is zero, has electric-force work $-dq\,\varphi_s$ by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-work]]; the balancing external work is $+dq\,\varphi_s$. Therefore $W_{\rm ext}=\int_0^1s\,ds\int\rho\varphi=\tfrac12\int\rho\varphi$. Both signs of $\rho$ are allowed. The symmetric double kernel gives the equivalent ordered-pair interpretation of the factor $1/2$.

(c) [Scope] the identity is a statement about the ideal quasi-static assembly of a compactly supported $C^1$ charge distribution in vacuum, all sources being held in place by external support ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]]). It asserts no time-dependent work, no radiation, no material or stability model, and it does not identify the field energy with the rest mass of any particle; the point-source limit is treated separately below and is divergent.

Statement

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set that is star-shaped with respect to some $a\in\Omega$ ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]), let $E:\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ be of class $C^1$ in the spatial vector-field sense of [[def-em-fields]] ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), and let $\rho:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be continuous — the fixed-time reading, in the sense of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]], of a pure electrostatic regime with the units and constant $\varepsilon_0>0$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]] ([[def-em-sources]]).
Suppose the reduced smooth-branch equations hold pointwise on $\Omega$:
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}E=0\qquad\text{on }\Omega,$$
with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]].
Then:

(a) [Closed field and potential] $-E$ is closed in the sense of [[def-closed-and-exact-c1-vector-fields]] — equivalently $\operatorname{curl}(-E)=0$ ([[cor-curl-vanishes-exactly-when-a-field-is-closed]]) — and the function
$$\varphi(x):=-\int_0^1E\bigl(a+s(x-a)\bigr)\cdot(x-a)\,ds$$
(the Euclidean inner product of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]) is a $C^2$ function on $\Omega$ with
$$\nabla\varphi=-E\qquad\text{on }\Omega$$
([[thm-poincare-lemma-for-star-shaped-domains]] applied to the closed $C^1$ field $-E$); continuity of the integrand and its first parameter derivatives and the proved identity $\nabla\varphi=-E$ with $E\in C^1$ give the stated regularity.

(b) [Poisson equation] with $\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}\nabla\varphi$ the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]],
$$-\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0}\qquad\text{pointwise on }\Omega.$$

(c) [Uniqueness up to constants] if $\psi\in C^2(\Omega)$ satisfies $\nabla\psi=-E$ on $\Omega$, then $\psi-\varphi$ is constant on $\Omega$; in particular $\varphi$ is uniquely determined by $\nabla\varphi=-E$ and one prescribed value. Star-shapedness gives path-connectedness through the centre $a$, so the constant is the same on all of $\Omega$ ([[cor-potentials-differ-by-a-componentwise-constant]], [[def-piecewise-c1-path-connected-conservative-and-path-independent]]).

No normalisation of $\varphi$ at infinity, and no boundary condition, is asserted on a general star-shaped $\Omega$; the additive constant remains free.

Define the **work of the electric force** along the prescribed path by the vector line integral
$$W(\gamma):=\int_\gamma qE\cdot d\mathbf r$$
of [[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]; $qE$ is the electric term of the external force adopted for a test charge in [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](i), and this identification of the electric term is a physical reading adopted with the coupling, not a decomposition derived in this item.
Then:

[F1] The pure electrostatic regime has $B=0$, $J=0$, time-independent fields and the reduced equations; on a star-shaped region the potential theorem provides $\varphi\in C^2(\Omega)$ with $\nabla\varphi=-E$ ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]], [[pthm-em-electrostatic-potential]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-sources]], [[def-em-si-conventions]], [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]).
claim:
Statement

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, star-shaped ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]) and the spatial region of a pure electrostatic regime as in [[pthm-em-electrostatic-potential]], with fields of [[def-em-fields]], charge parameters of [[def-em-sources]] and the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; thus $E:\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ is $C^1$, $B=0$ and $J=0$ ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]]), and by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-potential]] there is $\varphi\in C^2(\Omega)$ with $E=-\nabla\varphi$.
Let $q\in\mathbb R$ (coulombs) be the charge of a test particle and let $\gamma:[t_0,t_1]\to\Omega$ be a piecewise $C^1$ path ([[def-interval]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]).
Define the **work of the electric force** along the prescribed path by the vector line integral
$$W(\gamma):=\int_\gamma qE\cdot d\mathbf r$$
of [[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]; $qE$ is the electric term of the external force adopted for a test charge in [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](i), and this identification of the electric term is a physical reading adopted with the coupling, not a decomposition derived in this item.
Then:

(a) [Value] $W(\gamma)=q\,(\varphi(\gamma(t_0))-\varphi(\gamma(t_1)))$;

(b) [Path independence] if $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ are piecewise $C^1$ paths in $\Omega$ with the same initial and the same terminal point, then $W(\gamma_1)=W(\gamma_2)$; in particular $W(\gamma)=0$ for every closed piecewise $C^1$ path;

(c) [Potential energy] with the potential energy $U:=q\varphi$ (joules) the identity reads $W(\gamma)=-(U(\gamma(t_1))-U(\gamma(t_0)))$;

(d) [Gauge invariance of the work] if $\varphi' \in C^2(\Omega)$ is any other potential with $\nabla\varphi'=-E$, then $\varphi'=\varphi+c$ with a constant $c\in\mathbb R$ and the formula of (a) is unchanged ([[cor-potentials-differ-by-a-componentwise-constant]]).

The statement is a line-integral identity for a prescribed path in a prescribed static external field. It asserts no equation of motion, no radiation, no work done on the sources and no claim that the test particle actually follows $\gamma$; the interpretation of $W$ as work done by the adopted external coupling is the physical reading supplied by [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]], not a dynamical theorem.

claim:
Statement

Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of
[[def-em-lab-geometry]], with nonempty open time interval $I$
([[def-interval]]), positive constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and
$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. Define the **Gauss defects**

$$D_B:=\operatorname{div}B,\qquad D_E:=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0.$$

(a) [Smooth evolution branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^2$ fields and $\rho,J$
$C^1$ source fields of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]]. Assume only
the two evolution equations

$$\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E,\qquad\partial_tE=c^2\operatorname{curl}B-c^2\mu_0J,$$

and, separately, source continuity $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. No
Gauss constraint is assumed. Then $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ pointwise.
For each fixed $x$, both defects are constant on $I$. Initial zero constraints
at any $t_0\in I$ persist at every time; a nonzero defect at a point persists
with the same value. Thus evolution and continuity cannot repair a nonzero
initial Gauss defect.

(b) [Distributional evolution branch] The same derivative conclusion holds for
arbitrary scalar and vector distributions $E,B,\rho,J$ on $U$ satisfying the
two evolution identities and, independently, continuity in
$\mathcal D'(U)$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]).
This includes the original locally integrable field and source branch
identified with regular distributions and the declared singular-source class
when its equations hold. Thus $\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$
distributionally. If a defect has a continuous representative $h$ on $U$,
assume Countable Choice for the indicated Lebesgue integral and localization
interface ([[def-countable-choice]]); then $h(x,t)$ is independent of $t$. In
this continuous-representative case its zero or nonzero value at a time
persists. No restriction of an arbitrary distribution to a time slice is
assumed.

(c) [Full-Maxwell corollaries] Smooth solutions of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] satisfy the evolution and source-continuity
hypotheses by [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a), and their Gauss defects are
identically zero by the two Gauss equations. Its original locally integrable
weak branch has the same distributional conclusion. For admitted point and
stationary-sheet models under [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]],
[[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](b) supplies compatibility and the four
identities again give zero defects. Conversely, in (a), or in (b) when both
defects have continuous representatives, evolution plus continuity and zero
Gauss defects at one time give all four Maxwell identities on $U$, pointwise
in (a) and distributionally in (b).

This theorem is conditional on the stated equations and regularity. It proves
no existence, matter dynamics, observation or empirical fact. The derivative
algebra is choice-free; Countable Choice is confined to the
continuous-representative localization and the inherited declared
singular-source formulation.

$\partial_tE=c^2\operatorname{curl}B-c^2\mu_0J$ and, separately, the

$D_B=\operatorname{div}B$ and

$\partial_tD_B=\partial_tD_E=0$ pointwise; for each fixed $x$ both defects are

[F6] Parameter integrals ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]], set form): for
$K\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ compact, Lebesgue measurable with $\lambda_n(K)<\infty$
and $f$, $\partial_tf$ continuous on an open neighbourhood of $K\times[a,b]$,
the map $t\mapsto\int_Kf(x,t)\,dx$ is differentiable at every $t\in(a,b)$ with
derivative $\int_K\partial_tf(x,t)\,dx$, and has the corresponding one-sided
derivatives at the endpoints.

7.1 Moving-ball identity. Fix $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, $r_0>0$ and $t_0\le s\le t\le T$, put $r(v):=r_0+c(t-v)$ for $v\in[s,t]$ (so $r\ge r_0>0$ and $r'=-c$), and put $F(v):=\int_{B_{r(v)}(x_0)}u(x,v)\,dx$. For each $v$, the map $T_v(y)=x_0+r(v)y$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of $\mathbb R^3$ with $\det DT_v=r(v)^3$, and $T_v(B_1(0))=B_{r(v)}(x_0)$; by the change-of-variables lemma [F7] applied to the nonnegative Borel function $u(\cdot,v)$, $F(v)=\int_{B_1(0)}f(y,v)\,dy$ with $f(y,v):=u(x_0+r(v)y,v)r(v)^3$, and the boundary sphere $S^2$ is Lebesgue null by [F9], so the integral may equivalently be taken over the compact set $\overline B_1(0)$. On an open neighbourhood of $\overline B_1(0)\times[s,t]$ the function $f$ and its partial derivative $\partial_vf=\nabla u(x_0+ry,v)\cdot r'y\,r^3+\partial_vu(x_0+ry,v)\,r^3+3r^2r'u(x_0+ry,v)$ are continuous, because $u$ is $C^\infty$ in the extension sense and $r$ is $C^1$; the parameter-integral lemma [F6] with the compact finite-measure set $\overline B_1(0)$ therefore gives the one-sided derivatives at the endpoints and $F'(v)=\int_{\overline B_1(0)}\partial_vf(y,v)\,dy$ for $v\in(s,t)$. claim:
Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$,
[[def-countable-choice]]), inherited from
[[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]]. Let $t_0<T$ be real, let
$E_0,B_0:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^\infty$ fields
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) on the whole-space laboratory
region $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the
constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and assume the constraints
$$\operatorname{div}E_0=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B_0=0$$ on $\mathbb R^3$
([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]). Put
$\dot E_0:=c^2\operatorname{curl}B_0$ and
$\dot B_0:=-\operatorname{curl}E_0$. No decay, boundedness, compactness or
finite-energy hypothesis is imposed on the data. Then:

(a) [Existence and explicit representation] There are jointly $C^\infty$
fields $E,B:\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]\to\mathbb R^3$ (in the extension sense of
[[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]]) satisfying the four smooth-branch vacuum
Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with $\rho\equiv0$,
$J\equiv0$ and the initial conditions $E(\cdot,t_0)=E_0$,
$B(\cdot,t_0)=B_0$, $\partial_tE(\cdot,t_0)=\dot E_0$,
$\partial_tB(\cdot,t_0)=\dot B_0$. Explicitly, each component $E_i$ is the
scalar solution $u$ of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]](a) with data
$(a,b)=(E_{0,i},\dot E_{0,i})$ and $h=0$, each $B_i$ that with
$(a,b)=(B_{0,i},\dot B_{0,i})$, in the spherical-mean representation
$u=\partial_sH_a+H_b$ of that theorem, the mean being that of
[[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]].

(b) [Uniqueness] Every pair of jointly $C^2$ fields on
$\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ (in the extension sense) satisfying the same four
equations with $\rho\equiv0$, $J\equiv0$ and $E'(\cdot,t_0)=E_0$,
$B'(\cdot,t_0)=B_0$ equals $(E,B)$; the time derivatives at $t_0$ are then
automatically $\dot E_0,\dot B_0$ by the Ampere and Faraday equations.

(c) [Finite propagation and domain of dependence] If second constrained data
$(E_0',B_0')$ agree with $(E_0,B_0)$ together with all curls on the closed ball
$\overline B_{c(t_*-t_0)}(x_*)$ — that is, $E_0=E_0'$, $B_0=B_0'$,
$\operatorname{curl}E_0=\operatorname{curl}E_0'$ and
$\operatorname{curl}B_0=\operatorname{curl}B_0'$ there — then the
corresponding solutions agree at $(x_*,t_*)$, for all $x_*\in\mathbb R^3$ and
$t_*\in[t_0,T]$. Consequently the value at $(x_*,t_*)$ is determined by the
Cauchy data on the closed backward cone
$K(x_*,t_*)=\{(y,v):|y-x_*|\le c(t_*-v)\}$ of
[[def-forward-and-backward-wave-cones-domain-of-dependence-and-influence]]. In
the causal geometry of the adopted affine Minkowski model this cone is the
model's causal past cone of the event $(x_*,t_*)$ in the chart $x^0=ct$; by
the reachability objects of
[[def-sr-causal-reachability-in-affine-minkowski-space]] and the
straight-segment criterion and time monotonicity of
[[thm-sr-future-cone-and-flat-domain-of-dependence]], events outside it cannot
be joined to $(x_*,t_*)$ by a future causal path, so the constructed field
supplies no vacuum influence outside the model's causal cones; this
identification of the PDE cone with the model's causal cone is the modelling
statement of the item, not an additional empirical claim.

(d) [Compact support] If in addition $E_0$ and $B_0$ vanish off a compact set
$K\subset\mathbb R^3$, choose $\rho>0$ with $K\subseteq\overline B_\rho(0)$
([[thm-heine-borel-rn]]); then for every $t\in[t_0,T]$ one has
$E(x,t)=B(x,t)=0$ whenever $|x|>\rho+c(t-t_0)$.

(e) [Finite-energy branch] Define
$u(x,t)=(\varepsilon_0|E(x,t)|^2+\mu_0^{-1}|B(x,t)|^2)/2$ and
$S=\mu_0^{-1}E\times B$ as in [[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], and define total
energy by the nonnegative ball exhaustion
$\mathcal E(t):=\sup_{R>0}\int_{B_R(0)}u(x,t)\,dx\in[0,\infty]$. If
$\mathcal E(t_0)<\infty$, then $\mathcal E(t)=\mathcal E(t_0)$ for every
$t\in[t_0,T]$. More locally, for every $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, $r>0$ and
$t_0\le s\le t\le T$,
$$\int_{B_r(x_0)}u(x,t)\,dx\le\int_{B_{r+c(t-s)}(x_0)}u(x,s)\,dx.$$
This is a branch for the same smooth constrained data with finite initial
energy; no existence result for nonsmooth finite-energy data is asserted.

(f) [Scope] This is the smooth whole-space vacuum branch with initially
constraint-satisfying data; general smooth non-decaying data may have infinite
total energy, and no boundary condition, inhomogeneous source, weak-branch
content or empirical claim is asserted. The result is conditional on the
adopted postulates and on $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the latter used through the
scalar theorem and the divergence and substitution suppliers in clause (e).

1.2 Local integrability and distributional identities. $\varphi_I$ is locally integrable on $H$: $|x-p|^{-1}$ is locally integrable in dimension three and $|x+ae_3|^{-1}$ is continuous on $H$, and sums and scalar multiples of locally integrable measurable functions are locally integrable [F3]. On $H$ the second term is $C^\infty$ with classically vanishing Laplacian, so its distributional Laplacian is the regular distribution of the zero function [F2]; the first term has $-\Delta T=(q/\varepsilon_0)\delta_p$ on $\mathbb R^3$, hence on the open subset $H$ [F1]. $$-\Delta T_{\varphi_I}=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\,\delta_p\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(H),$$

(f) [Scope] the statement concerns the ideal point charge above an ideal grounded plane in the declared decay class; it excludes finite-plane edge effects, conductor thickness, transients, moving charges, radiation, self-force and any measurement; no uniqueness is asserted outside the class of (d), and the point-source singularity is never evaluated.

Statement

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ be the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $j_1,\dots,j_n\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}j_\alpha=0$ be fixed compact smooth conserved current profiles of the class of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](b), extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$. Fix amplitudes $I\in\mathbb R^n$, put $J_I:=\sum_{\alpha=1}^nI_\alpha j_\alpha$, let $A_{J_I}$ be the Coulomb-gauge Newtonian vector potential of [[pthm-em-magnetostatic-vector-potential]] applied to the conserved current $J_I$, and let $B_{J_I}=\operatorname{curl}A_{J_I}$. Define the linkage coefficients
$$L_{\alpha\beta}:=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\langle j_\alpha(x),j_\beta(y)\rangle}{|x-y|}\,d\lambda_3(y)\,d\lambda_3(x),\qquad\alpha,\beta=1,\dots,n .$$
Then:

(a) [Finiteness and self-energy] every $L_{\alpha\beta}$ is a finite real number: the defining double integral converges absolutely, and in particular every self-coefficient $L_{\alpha\alpha}$ is finite, so the compact smooth profiles carry a finite self-energy. This is a statement about the smooth profiles only; no finite value is assigned to a zero-radius thin-wire self-inductance.

(b) [Reciprocity and flux linkage] $L_{\alpha\beta}=L_{\beta\alpha}$ for all $\alpha,\beta$; $A_{J_I}=\sum_{\alpha}I_\alpha A_{j_\alpha}$ componentwise; and for every $\beta$ the linkage integral is
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\langle j_\beta,A_{J_I}\rangle\,d\lambda_3=\sum_{\alpha=1}^nL_{\beta\alpha}I_\alpha .$$
Thus the numbers $L_{\alpha\beta}$ are the linkage coefficients of the profiles: the linkage of profile $\beta$ with the field of the superposition is the linear combination $\sum_\alpha L_{\beta\alpha}I_\alpha$.

(c) [Magnetic energy and positivity] with $U(I):=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}\langle J_I,A_{J_I}\rangle\,d\lambda_3$,
$$U(I)=\frac12\sum_{\alpha,\beta=1}^nL_{\alpha\beta}I_\alpha I_\beta=\frac1{2\mu_0}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|B_{J_I}|^2\,d\lambda_3\ \ge0,$$
all quantities finite; moreover $U(I)=0$ holds precisely when $J_I=0$ on $\mathbb R^3$. Consequently the symmetric matrix $L=(L_{\alpha\beta})$ is positive semidefinite, and it is positive definite exactly when the profiles are pointwise linearly independent, i.e. when $\sum_\alpha I_\alpha j_\alpha\equiv0$ forces $I=0$.

(d) [Scope] the theorem concerns fixed compact smooth conserved current profiles and their Coulomb-gauge fields. It asserts no thin-wire, sheet or singular self-inductance; no time-dependent, moving, radiating or material configuration; and no uniqueness of the vector potential. The identification of these coefficients with the inductance matrix of the adopted lumped circuit model, and of the linkage derivatives with terminal voltages, is adopted in [[post-em-circuit-approximation]]; the strict material-loop theorem applies separately only to an actual moving sheet and compatible smooth Maxwell fields satisfying its hypotheses. No terminal-voltage law for arbitrary varying frozen profiles is inferred from the present magnetostatic computation.

surface_related_text: Assume the lumped circuit model of [[post-em-circuit-approximation]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]) for clause (b), where it is inherited from the linkage suppliers.

(a) [Terminal-energy bookkeeping] Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval ([[def-interval]]), let $t_0,t_1\in J$, let $L\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be constant and symmetric, let $I:J\to\mathbb R^n$ be of class $C^1$ in the following sense: $I$ extends to a $C^1$ map on an open interval containing $J$, so that the derivatives used below are those of the extension (one-sided at included endpoints of $J$, and not intrinsic to a value restriction when $J$ is a singleton), and let $V(t):=L\dot I(t)$ be the terminal-voltage vector of the inductive branches as adopted in [[post-em-circuit-approximation]] (the Faraday branch: the terminal voltage of a branch is the rate of change of its flux linkage $\Phi=LI$). Then
$$\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\langle V(t),I(t)\rangle\,dt=\frac12\langle I(t_1),LI(t_1)\rangle-\frac12\langle I(t_0),LI(t_0)\rangle ,$$
and for $n=1$ with $L>0$ this reads $\int_{t_0}^{t_1}V I\,dt=\frac12L\bigl(I(t_1)^2-I(t_0)^2\bigr)$: the accumulated terminal energy equals the change of the inductor bookkeeping energy $\frac12LI^2$. The identity is exact for every such $C^1$ current and fixed geometry; it uses only symmetry of $L$, the product rule and the fundamental theorem of calculus. For a changing geometry the mechanical work done on the circuit is an additional term and is not covered here.

(b) [Identification with the frozen field energy] Suppose in addition that the currents are realized by fixed compact smooth conserved profiles $j_1,\dots,j_n$ of the class of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](b), with instantaneous source $J(t):=\sum_\alpha I_\alpha(t)j_\alpha$, and that the inductance matrix is the linkage matrix of those profiles in the sense of [[pthm-em-inductance-reciprocity]]: $L_{\alpha\beta}=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\iint\frac{\langle j_\alpha(x),j_\beta(y)\rangle}{|x-y|}\,d\lambda_3(y)\,d\lambda_3(x)$. Then for every $t\in J$
$$\frac12\langle I(t),LI(t)\rangle=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}\langle J(t),A_{J(t)}\rangle\,d\lambda_3=\frac1{2\mu_0}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|B_{J(t)}|^2\,d\lambda_3\ \ge0,$$
where $A_{J(t)}$ is the Coulomb-gauge Newtonian vector potential and $B_{J(t)}=\operatorname{curl}A_{J(t)}$ of that theorem: the right-hand side is the magnetic field energy of the frozen instantaneous configuration, and the accumulated terminal energy of (a) between $t_0$ and $t_1$ is the change of this field energy. The relation $V=L\dot I$ is the explicitly adopted terminal law of [[post-em-circuit-approximation]]; the identification of the model's inductance matrix with the smooth-profile linkage matrix is part of the adopted model of [[post-em-circuit-approximation]].

**Given:** Assume the lumped model data of [[post-em-circuit-approximation]], a constant symmetric $L\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, an interval $J$, points $t_0,t_1\in J$, a current $I:J\to\mathbb R^n$ extending to a $C^1$ map on an open interval containing $J$, the terminal voltage $V=L\dot I$, and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for clause (b).

[F1] The adopted lumped circuit model carries branch currents $I_\alpha:J\to\mathbb R$ and constant matrices $L,C,R$ with $L$ symmetric, the Faraday branch relation $V(t)=L\dot I(t)$ (each terminal potential is the rate of change of the branch flux linkage $LI$), and the circuit-level bookkeeping quantities $LI$, $\tfrac12I^{\mathsf T}LI$; the matrices, terminal geometry and loop choice are declared model data, not derived from the vacuum Maxwell equations. ([[post-em-circuit-approximation]]).

[F5] If $a<b$, $G:[a,b]\to\mathbb R$ is differentiable at every point of $[a,b]$ as a function on $[a,b]$ (one-sided at the endpoints), and $G'$ is integrable on $[a,b]$, then $\int_a^bG'=G(b)-G(a)$. ([[thm-ftc-second-part]]).

[F7] For fixed compact smooth conserved profiles $j_1,\dots,j_n$ the linkage coefficients $L_{\alpha\beta}=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\iint\langle j_\alpha(x),j_\beta(y)\rangle/|x-y|$ are finite real numbers with $L_{\alpha\beta}=L_{\beta\alpha}$, the linkage of the superposition is $\int\langle j_\beta,A_{J_I}\rangle=\sum_\alpha L_{\beta\alpha}I_\alpha$, and with $U(I):=\frac12\int\langle J_I,A_{J_I}\rangle$ one has $U(I)=\frac12\sum_{\alpha,\beta}L_{\alpha\beta}I_\alpha I_\beta=\frac1{2\mu_0}\int|B_{J_I}|^2\ge0$, with $U(I)=0$ exactly when $J_I=0$. ([[pthm-em-inductance-reciprocity]]).

[F8] The compact smooth current class consists of the currents $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$, extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$. ([[def-em-steady-current-regime]]).

2.1 Let $u:=\min\{t_0,t_1\}$ and $v:=\max\{t_0,t_1\}$; then $[u,v]\subseteq J$, since $J$ is order-convex by [F2] and contains both $u$ and $v$. If $u<v$, then $G$ is differentiable at every point of $[u,v]$ as a function on $[u,v]$ (interior points lie in the open set $U$, and at $u,v$ the one-sided derivatives exist by restriction of the extension), while $G'$ is continuous on $[u,v]$ by step 1.1 and hence integrable there by [F4]; [F5] gives $\int_u^vG'=G(v)-G(u)$, that is $\int_u^v\langle V,I\rangle=G(v)-G(u)$ by step 1.1. If $u=v$ the same display is $0=G(v)-G(u)$, which holds identically and is the $u=v$ reading of [F6]. If $t_0>t_1$, applying the already-proved case to the pair $(t_1,t_0)$ and the sign clause of [F6] gives $\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\langle V,I\rangle=-\int_{t_1}^{t_0}\langle V,I\rangle=-(G(t_0)-G(t_1))=G(t_1)-G(t_0)$. In every case $\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\langle V(t),I(t)\rangle\,dt=\frac12\langle I(t_1),LI(t_1)\rangle-\frac12\langle I(t_0),LI(t_0)\rangle$, which is the identity of (a); for $n=1$ the quadratic form is $\frac12LI^2$ by [F10]. [F2, F4, F5, F6, F10, step 1.1, algebra, cases]

Fitzpatrick §7.5, printed pp. 225-231, writes the battery work for coupled coils as Ohmic terms plus the inductive energy and states that the energy of an inductor is stored in the magnetic field; Tong §4.1.2, printed pp. 71-73, integrates the work against the induced emf to $W=\frac12LI^2$ and rewrites it as the magnetostatic field energy under a decay assumption; Griffiths §7.2.4, printed pp. 317-320, records $\frac12LI^2$ and $U=\frac1{2\mu_0}\int B^2\,d\tau$. The present theorem replaces the decay assumption by the compact smooth conservative profiles of [[pthm-em-inductance-reciprocity]] and keeps the terminal law and the matrix identification as explicitly adopted model content; no error bound and no singular thin-wire self-inductance are claimed.
