Statement

Assume the lumped circuit model of [[post-em-circuit-approximation]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]) for clause (b), where it is inherited from the linkage suppliers.

(a) [Terminal-energy bookkeeping] Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval ([[def-interval]]), let $t_0,t_1\in J$, let $L\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be constant and symmetric, let $I:J\to\mathbb R^n$ be of class $C^1$ in the following sense: $I$ extends to a $C^1$ map on an open interval containing $J$, so that the derivatives used below are those of the extension (one-sided at included endpoints of $J$, and not intrinsic to a value restriction when $J$ is a singleton), and let $V(t):=L\dot I(t)$ be the terminal-voltage vector of the inductive branches as adopted in [[post-em-circuit-approximation]] (the Faraday branch: the terminal voltage of a branch is the rate of change of its flux linkage $\Phi=LI$). Then
$$\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\langle V(t),I(t)\rangle\,dt=\frac12\langle I(t_1),LI(t_1)\rangle-\frac12\langle I(t_0),LI(t_0)\rangle ,$$
and for $n=1$ with $L>0$ this reads $\int_{t_0}^{t_1}V I\,dt=\frac12L\bigl(I(t_1)^2-I(t_0)^2\bigr)$: the accumulated terminal energy equals the change of the inductor bookkeeping energy $\frac12LI^2$. The identity is exact for every such $C^1$ current and fixed geometry; it uses only symmetry of $L$, the product rule and the fundamental theorem of calculus. For a changing geometry the mechanical work done on the circuit is an additional term and is not covered here.

(b) [Identification with the frozen field energy] Suppose in addition that the currents are realized by fixed compact smooth conserved profiles $j_1,\dots,j_n$ of the class of [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](b), with instantaneous source $J(t):=\sum_\alpha I_\alpha(t)j_\alpha$, and that the inductance matrix is the linkage matrix of those profiles in the sense of [[pthm-em-inductance-reciprocity]]: $L_{\alpha\beta}=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\iint\frac{\langle j_\alpha(x),j_\beta(y)\rangle}{|x-y|}\,d\lambda_3(y)\,d\lambda_3(x)$. Then for every $t\in J$
$$\frac12\langle I(t),LI(t)\rangle=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3}\langle J(t),A_{J(t)}\rangle\,d\lambda_3=\frac1{2\mu_0}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|B_{J(t)}|^2\,d\lambda_3\ \ge0,$$
where $A_{J(t)}$ is the Coulomb-gauge Newtonian vector potential and $B_{J(t)}=\operatorname{curl}A_{J(t)}$ of that theorem: the right-hand side is the magnetic field energy of the frozen instantaneous configuration, and the accumulated terminal energy of (a) between $t_0$ and $t_1$ is the change of this field energy. The relation $V=L\dot I$ is the explicitly adopted terminal law of [[post-em-circuit-approximation]]; the identification of the model's inductance matrix with the smooth-profile linkage matrix is part of the adopted model of [[post-em-circuit-approximation]].

(c) [Scope] no radiation, distributed-element, material-loss, moving-geometry or thin-wire self-inductance claim is made; the frozen-configuration energy is not asserted to be the energy of a time-dependent full Maxwell solution.

surface_related_text: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $q\in\mathbb R$, let $z,v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline, $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), let $s_0$ be an emission event with $z'(s_0)=0$ (the charge is momentarily at rest in the laboratory chart), and put $a:=z''(s_0)$ and, for $n\in S^2$, $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$. Let $E,B$ be the retarded fields of the charge given by [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] and $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Then:

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]); the laboratory chart, units and constants of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]]; a retarded point-geometry datum with the off-worldline retarded data $s,r,n,\beta,\kappa,\dot\beta$ of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] and the point charge parameter $q$, $C=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$; the retarded fields $E,B$ of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] with $S=E\times B/\mu_0$; the rest event $s_0$ with $z'(s_0)=0$, $a=z''(s_0)$, and in clause (f) a general emission event with $\beta_0=z'(s_0)/c$, $|\beta_0|\le v_*/c$, $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot\beta_0$.

[F1] Lienard-Wiechert point fields: off the worldline $E=E_{\mathrm{vel}}+E_{\mathrm{acc}}$ with $E_{\mathrm{vel}}=C(1-|\beta|^{2})(n-\beta)/(\kappa^{3}r^{2})$, $E_{\mathrm{acc}}=C\,n\times((n-\beta)\times\dot\beta)/(c\kappa^{3}r)$, $B=n\times E/c$, $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$; at an emission event $(x_r,t_r)=(z(s_0)+rn,s_0+r/c)$ the retarded data are $\beta_0,\dot\beta_0=a/c,\kappa_0$ and $r$, and the same formulas and remainder bound hold there. ([[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] (b),(c))
[F2] Retarded emission geometry: $(x_r,t_r)$ lies off the worldline, $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$, $r>0$, $\kappa_0=1-n\cdot\beta_0\in[1-v_*/c,1+v_*/c]$. ([[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (b),(c))

8.1 Scope and conclusion (e). At a rest event $z'(s_0)=0$ one has $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot 0=1$ for every $n\in S^2$ [F2], so the emission-time Jacobian is identically $1$ and no retarded-time conversion factor appears: the limits of (b) are simultaneously the fixed-sphere flux and the emitted power per unit emission time, and the angular and total powers of (c)-(d) are the emitted quantities of the rest event. The computation used only the prescribed worldline, the retarded model fields and the adopted causal selection of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] and [[post-em-radiation-selection]]; it forms no product of distributions, asserts no self-force, radiation reaction, mass derivation or mechanical evolution law, and makes no empirical or measurement claim, while clause (f) records the general low-speed comparison as a separate quantified statement rather than a loss law. Steps 1.1-7.1 together with this clause prove (a)-(f). [step 1.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, step 7.1, F2, F5, F10, algebra] ∎
claim:
Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $q\in\mathbb R$, let $z,v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline, $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), let $s_0$ be an emission event with $z'(s_0)=0$ (the charge is momentarily at rest in the laboratory chart), and put $a:=z''(s_0)$ and, for $n\in S^2$, $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$. Let $E,B$ be the retarded fields of the charge given by [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] and $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Then:

(a) [Field on the emitted sphere] For every $r>0$ and $n\in S^2$, $$E(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C\,n\times(n\times a)}{c^2r}+\rho_E(s_0,n,r),\qquad|\rho_E(s_0,n,r)|\le|C|\frac{1+v_*/c}{(1-v_*/c)^3}r^{-2},\qquad B(x_r,t_r)=\frac{n\times E(x_r,t_r)}{c}.$$

(b) [Angular flux density] The limits $$\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n):=\lim_{r\to\infty}r^2\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C^{2}\,|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}},\qquad P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\int_{S^2}\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n)\,d\sigma(n),$$ exist with the convergence uniform in $n\in S^2$; $d\sigma$ is the polar surface measure of the unit sphere (equal to the chart surface measure by [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]).

(c) [Total power] $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\cdot\frac{8\pi}{3}|a|^{2}=\frac{q^2|a|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ the Larmor power of the momentarily resting prescribed charge.

(d) [Angular distribution] Writing $\theta$ for the angle between $n$ and $a$ (with $\theta$ undefined only when $a=0$, in which case $dP/d\sigma\equiv0$), $$\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n)=\frac{q^2|a|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\sin^2\theta:$$ the radiation pattern vanishes along the instantaneous acceleration axis and is maximal in the perpendicular plane; $\int_{S^2}dP/d\sigma\,d\sigma=P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$. If $a=0$ all displayed radiation quantities vanish.

(e) [Scope and conventions] The result is exact at an emission event at which the charge is instantaneously at rest in the laboratory chart: then $\kappa_0(n)=1$ for every $n$, so no retarded-time conversion factor appears and the displayed limits are simultaneously the fixed-sphere flux and the emitted power per unit emission time. The item uses only the prescribed worldline and the retarded model fields -- it is not a mechanical evolution law, does not assert a self-force or radiation reaction, derives no mass, and makes no empirical or measurement claim. For a general emission event the exact formula and its low-speed comparison are supplied by clause (f); 'slow' motion alone is never substituted for an error bound. The prescribed curve, the uniform subluminal bound and $z'(s_0)=0$ are hypotheses; for a varying-velocity worldline the instantaneous rest event is a single parameter value, not an interval.

(f) [General low-speed branch] At any emission event, without imposing $z'(s_0)=0$ for this clause, define emitted power by the weighted far-zone flux integral $\kappa_0(n)\,r^2\,n\cdot S$ on the emitted spheres, with $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot\beta_0$, $\beta_0=z'(s_0)/c$ and $|\beta_0|\le v_*/c$. The same field formula and angular computation give $$P_{\mathrm{em}}=\gamma_0^{6}\bigl(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2}\bigr)\frac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}.$$ Put $P_{\mathrm L}=q^{2}|a|^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$. For $|\beta_0|\le\delta<1$, $$P_{\mathrm L}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}\le(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L},\qquad |P_{\mathrm{em}}-P_{\mathrm L}|\le3\delta^{2}(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L}.$$ This includes $q=0$ or $a=0$ without division by $P_{\mathrm L}$. Uniform angular comparison is also explicit: if $N_\beta=n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)$, $N_0=n\times(n\times a)$ and $H_\beta=q^{2}|N_\beta|^{2}/(16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3}\kappa_0^{5})$, $H_0=q^{2}|N_0|^{2}/(16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3})$, then $$|H_\beta-H_0|\le\frac{q^2|a|^2}{16\pi^2\varepsilon_0c^3}\,\delta\left[\frac{2+\delta}{(1-\delta)^5}+\frac{5}{(1-\delta)^6}\right]$$ for all $n$. The exact rest-event clauses (a)-(e) retain their hypotheses; this additional branch supplies the general low-speed comparison, not a mechanical loss law.

Let the setting be that of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]]: a charge $q\in\mathbb R$ ($C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$) on a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline $z$ in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], with retarded fields $E,B$ off the worldline and the uniform far-zone remainder of that item; let $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]). Define the **emitted power at the emission event $s_0$** by the $\kappa_0$-weighted far-zone flux

(b) [Closed form and four-acceleration form] If $b:=|\beta_0|<1$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp$ is decomposed along $\beta_0=|\beta_0|e_3$ and perpendicular to it, then $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{q^{2}\gamma_0^{6}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\bigl(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2}\bigr)=\frac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\,\eta(A,A),$$ where $A$ is the four-acceleration of the worldline at $s_0$ and $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](e)). [F1] Emitted-power branch: for a general emission event the $\kappa_0$-weighted far-zone flux has the limit $P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\int_{S^2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}\kappa_0^{-5}d\sigma$ (the uniform pointwise convergence and the interchange of limit and integral being established in its proof), and this equals $\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})q^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$; for $|\beta_0|\le\delta<1$ it satisfies $P_{\mathrm L}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}\le(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L}$ and $|P_{\mathrm{em}}-P_{\mathrm L}|\le3\delta^{2}(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}P_{\mathrm L}$ with $P_{\mathrm L}=q^{2}|a|^{2}/(6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3})$, and at $\beta_0=0$ it reduces to the exact rest-event Larmor power. ([[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]] (a)-(d),(f))

[F2] Point fields and remainder: on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, $E=E_{\mathrm{vel}}+E_{\mathrm{acc}}$, $B=n\times E/c$, with the velocity part $O(r^{-2})$ bounded by $|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$ and the acceleration part the leading term; at $(x_r,t_r)$ the retarded data are those of the emission event and $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$. ([[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] (b),(c), [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]] (c),(d))
[F4] Retarded root: $\partial_ts=1/\kappa$ off the worldline, and $\kappa_0(n)=1-n\cdot\beta_0\in[1-v_*/c,1+v_*/c]$. ([[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (a),(b))

surface_related_text: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the point-source change-of-variables suppliers below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]] ($c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$), let $q\in\mathbb R$ and let $z$, $v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline of a point charge, [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], with the constant $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), and let $\rho,J$ be the point-source distributions of that charge on the worldline in the declared point-source class of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) (the $C^3$ branch of the point-current construction). Let $(\varphi,A)$ be the retarded history pairings of [[lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields]](b) -- the framework's retarded construction for this source under the adopted selection [[post-em-radiation-selection]] -- and define $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\nabla\times A$ on the off-worldline domain $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]). Then:

(a) [Potentials] $\varphi=C/(\kappa r)$ and $A=\beta\varphi/c$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, where $r,\kappa,\beta$ are the retarded data of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]](b); the zero extensions of $\varphi,A$ to $\Gamma$ are locally integrable on $\Omega$.

(d) [Scope] These are the stipulated retarded model fields of the prescribed charge: the item identifies, through the same adopted causal selection used by [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]] for the compact branch, the point-source potentials and fields of the model, and proves their exact form and bounds. It asserts no value of the fields on the worldline $\Gamma$ (where the formulas are undefined and the self-field is singular), no integral or energy statement, no self-force and no radiation reaction, and derives no mass. The uniform bound $v_*<c$ and the exclusion of $\Gamma$ are essential hypotheses; the companion example page shows that a merely pointwise subluminal curve can fail to have a retarded root, and no uniformity in the emission event $s_0$ is claimed ($z''$ is not assumed bounded). The signed constant $C$ is retained in every displayed formula while absolute-value bounds use $|C|$.

(e) [Constructed weak solution] Let $\Phi,\Upsilon$ be the global regular potential distributions in (a), and let $\mathcal E=-\nabla\Phi-\partial_t\Upsilon$, $\mathcal B=\operatorname{curl}\Upsilon$. By [[thm-em-retarded-point-distributional-maxwell]], their representatives are exactly the locally integrable zero extensions of the displayed off-worldline fields. They satisfy all four identities of [[def-em-weak-sources]](e) with the proper all-time point pair $\rho,J$; the volume source parts are zero. Thus they are an admitted point-source model of the explicit physical adoption [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], under the same retarded selection. The potentials satisfy $W\Phi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $W\Upsilon=\mu_0J$ and the distributional Lorenz identity. This existence and solution property is supplied by the mathematical theorem, not by the selection postulate or by the compact-source theorem. The zero extensions on the null graph give no physically defined self-field and no nonlinear products there. All original exact field, regularity and uniform far-zone branches remain as stated. On each product neighborhood disjoint from $\Gamma$ the fields satisfy the smooth source-free Maxwell equations. Consequently any use of [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]] by the radiation items is local on such neighborhoods, with $\rho=J=0$; it neither applies that smooth theorem across the point source nor forms self-work or a global finite-energy identity.

Let $\gamma:[0,L]\to\mathbb R^3$ be a $C^2$ curve parametrized by arc length ($|\gamma'|\equiv1$) that is either closed ($\gamma(0)=\gamma(L)$ with matching one-sided derivatives) or a wire segment with free endpoints, let $I\in\mathbb R$, let $m=\frac I2\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\gamma'(s)\,ds$ be the finite Riemann source moment defined by this displayed integral in the closed case. For an embedded closed loop this agrees with [[def-em-magnetic-moment]](b); embeddedness is not required for the present parametrized-curve calculation. Let $B$ be a prescribed external magnetic field, of class $C^0$ on a neighbourhood of the trace of $\gamma$ in part (a) and of class $C^2$ on an open set containing the closed ball $\overline{B_a(0)}$ in parts (b)-(d). Adopt the thin-wire coupling hypothesis (W): for a general closed parametrized curve use the stated direct neutral-wire Riemann coupling (with multiplicity of traversal retained); in the embedded closed-loop specialization its source interpretation is exactly [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](c1); for an open curve use a compact segment of a fed or closed neutral circuit, including a segment of the declared infinite wire of (c2). Adopt separately for that parametrized wire or local segment the direct external magnetic coupling $dF=I\,d\gamma\times B$ and $dN=\gamma\times dF$, as an ideal extension motivated by the smooth continuum Lorentz law [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]](ii); that smooth-source postulate does not itself include singular currents. An isolated static neutral open segment is not asserted: its standalone current satisfies $\operatorname{div}J_{\rm seg}=I(\delta_{\gamma(0)}-\delta_{\gamma(L)})$, so its endpoint feed/return cannot be suppressed in a global model. Force and torque here concern only the specified local segment under this adopted coupling. Then:

**(a) [Force and torque under (W)]**
$$F:=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\,ds,\qquad N:=I\int_0^L\gamma(s)\times\bigl(\gamma'(s)\times B(\gamma(s))\bigr)\,ds,$$
the componentwise Riemann integrals of continuous functions on the compact interval $[0,L]$ ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]).

**(b) [Constant field]** If $\gamma$ is closed and $B$ is constant on a neighbourhood of the loop, then $F=0$ and $N=m\times B$ exactly.

**(c) [Slowly varying field]** Let $\gamma$ be closed with $|\gamma(s)|\le a$ for all $s$, let $B$ be $C^2$ on an open set containing $\overline{B_a(0)}$ with constants $M_1,M_2$ such that $|B(x)-B(y)|\le M_1|x-y|$ and $|B(x)-B(0)-DB(0)x|\le\frac12M_2|x|^2$ for $|x|,|y|\le a$, and suppose $\operatorname{div}B=0$ on $B_a(0)$ (as holds for the external part of any smooth-branch vacuum field by [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]). $$F=\nabla(m\cdot B)(0)+R_F,\qquad N=m\times B(0)+R_N,$$
with $|R_F|\le\frac12|I|\,L\,a^2M_2$ and $|R_N|\le|I|\,L\,a^2M_1$, where $\nabla(m\cdot B)(0)$ is the gradient at $0$ of $x\mapsto m\cdot B(x)$ for the fixed vector $m$ ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

**(e) [Scope]** Only the external field acts on the loop: the loop's own field, self-force, radiation reaction, mechanical support and material response are outside the statement, and no claim is made about the loop's dynamics, deformation or failure. The coupling (W) is an explicit idealisation of a neutral thin wire at rest in the laboratory frame; it is adopted, not derived, and the theorem is conditional on it. No measurement or uncertainty is involved. Parts (a)-(c), conditional on the explicit coupling (W) and the supplied curve and external field, are finite Riemann-integral calculations and use no Choice axiom. Part (d), transporting the Newtonian-potential construction, assumes Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

Write $[F]=F_+-F_-$ for the jump of the one-sided traces.

**[Thin-interface hypothesis]** Suppose that $E,B,D,H$ satisfy the four macroscopic equations of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] in the distributional sense on $U$ with the source pair $\rho_f=\rho_v+\sigma_f\delta_S$, $J_f=J_v+K_f\delta_S$, where the stationary-sheet pairings are those of [[def-em-weak-sources]](c) and the equations are $\operatorname{div}D=\rho_f$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$, $\operatorname{curl}H=J_f+\partial_tD$ as identities in the sense of [[def-distribution]], the fields being identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and $\psi$ ranging over $C_c^\infty(U)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). **[Weak-trace branch]** If instead of the joint extension hypothesis the fields have the original one-sided spatial $C^1$ extensions at each time and, in addition, the piecewise first spatial and temporal derivatives are in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(U)$ and the one-sided field traces are measurable and locally integrable on $S\times I$ with respect to $dS\,dt$, then the same four identities hold as identities of sheet distributions and for $dS\,dt$-almost every $(x,t)$; since the traces are spatially continuous at each fixed time, they hold for every $x\in S$ for almost every $t$, and at every $(x,t)$ whenever the jump densities are additionally jointly continuous. No existence theorem for fields with singular sources is asserted, no constitutive law is used, and no empirical claim is made.

On the infinite straight rectangular guide $Q=(0,a)\times(0,b)\times\mathbb R$ of [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]], declare the finite-energy reflection class as follows. Extend in the two transverse variables to $T_{ab}^2\times\mathbb R$, $T_{ab}^2=\mathbb R/(2a\mathbb Z)\times\mathbb R/(2b\mathbb Z)$. The electric components have transverse parities even/odd, odd/even, odd/odd respectively; magnetic components have odd/even, even/odd, even/even respectively. For smooth fields this gives the four-wall conditions $n\times E=0$, $n\cdot B=0$; it is a precise weak PEC realization, not an assertion about every rough trace class. (a) [Complete mixed transform] Let $\phi_{mn}(x_t)=(4ab)^{-1/2}e^{i\pi(mx_1/a+nx_2/b)}$, $(m,n)\in\mathbb Z^2$, be the orthonormal transverse characters. For each component first form $F_{mn}(z)=\int_{T_{ab}^2}F(x_t,z)\overline{\phi_{mn}(x_t)}\,dx_t$, then apply the exact negative-sign $2\pi$ Fourier transform $\mathcal F_2$ of [[thm-plancherel]] in $z$. Write $\widehat F_{mn}(\xi)=\mathcal F_2F_{mn}(\xi)$ and $\beta=2\pi\xi$. The transform is a unitary representation of $L^2(T_{ab}^2\times\mathbb R)$ by $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^2;L^2(\mathbb R))$, with inverse in $L^2$ from [[thm-l-two-fourier-inversion]], and $$\|F\|_{L^2(Q)}^2=\tfrac14\sum_{m,n}\int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat F_{mn}(\xi)|^2\,d\xi$$ for these reflection fields. The parity and reality relations are retained, including $\widehat F_{-m,-n}(-\xi)=\overline{\widehat F_{mn}(\xi)}$. With $K=(\pi m/a,\pi n/b,2\pi\xi)$, the divergence constraints become $K\cdot\widehat E=K\cdot\widehat B=0$ for almost every $\xi$. This is a complete transverse sin/cos and longitudinal $L^2$ Fourier representation, not pointwise Fourier convergence or a finite-energy monochromatic plane wave.
(b) [Unique energy evolution] Adopt in that weak reflection class the constant-Ohmic first-order material evolution $E_t=v^2\operatorname{curl}B-\gamma E$, $B_t=-\operatorname{curl}E$, distributionally, consistent with the smooth [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]] and [[pthm-em-restricted-material-energy]] branches. For every initial pair in the class there is a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2(Q))$ solution in the same class. Its mixed coefficients solve, for every transverse index and almost every $\xi$, $$\partial_t\widehat E=iv^2K\times\widehat B-\gamma\widehat E,\qquad\partial_t\widehat B=-iK\times\widehat E.$$ Finite transverse sums and bounded longitudinal frequency truncations reconstruct the solution in energy norm uniformly on compact time intervals; such reconstructed fields are dense in the class at every time. They retain the divergence constraints and the original parities, including zero coefficient cases without dividing by $K$ or $|K|$.
(c) [Energy and dispersion] The total stored energy of this whole infinite guide is finite and equals $$\mathcal U(t)=\tfrac18\sum_{m,n}\int_{\mathbb R}(\varepsilon|\widehat E|^2+\mu^{-1}|\widehat B|^2)\,d\xi.$$ For every $t_0<t_1$, $\mathcal U(t_1)+\sigma\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\|E(t)\|_{L^2(Q)}^2dt=\mathcal U(t_0)$, and $\mathcal U'(t)=-\sigma\|E(t)\|_2^2$. At $\sigma=0$ energy is conserved and each constrained electric coefficient satisfies $\widehat E''+v^2|K|^2\widehat E=0$, so $\omega^2=v^2[(\pi m/a)^2+(\pi n/b)^2+\beta^2]$. These are the exact finite transverse-mode matrices of the approved K10 branch; individual separated TE/TM candidate fields still have their own cutoff and zero-profile restrictions, and no TE$_{00}$ mode is created by a scalar constant coefficient. Its full-Choice smooth-cavity realization is not used. At $K=0$ keep the direct first-order equations $\widehat E\prime=-\gamma\widehat E$, $\widehat B\prime=0$, without dividing by $K$; the original parity and $L^2$ relations still apply. No signal-speed or empirical inference is made.
(d) [Scope] This theorem supplies the previously missing complete longitudinal $L^2$ expansion of the declared straight rectangular guide, including its lossless and constant-Ohmic energy evolutions. It makes no completeness claim for arbitrary non-rectangular, dispersive, nonlocal, nonlinear, rough-wall or open-end/junction problems. The weak energy result is proved by linear mixed-transform evolution and modal limits, not by applying a nonlinear smooth Poynting identity to rough data.

From the phasor equations and [F6], $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E'=i\omega\operatorname{curl}\widetilde B'=i\omega(-i\omega c^{-2}\widetilde E')=\omega^2c^{-2}\widetilde E'=k^2\widetilde E'$ and $\operatorname{div}\widetilde E'=0$, so [F6] gives $\nabla\operatorname{div}\widetilde E'-\Delta\widetilde E'=-\Delta\widetilde E'=k^2\widetilde E'$, that is $(\Delta+k^2)\widetilde E'=0$ on $D$. The restriction of $\widetilde E'$ to $\overline D$ is $C^\infty$, has tangential trace $e_T$, divergence zero and the same modal outgoing condition on $S_R$; all hypotheses of the uniqueness clause of [F1] are therefore satisfied, and $\widetilde E'=\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ on $D$. Then $\widetilde B'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E'=(i\omega)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}\widetilde E_{\rm scat}=\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$ on $D$ by the third phasor equation and the definition of $\widetilde B_{\rm scat}$. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F6, algebra]

For the associated real field, the tangential projection of $E_{\rm tot}(x,t)=\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E_{\rm tot}(x)e^{-i\omega t})$ is $\operatorname{Re}(\widetilde E_{\rm tot,tang}(x)e^{-i\omega t})=0$ by the real-linearity of the projection [F7] and of $\operatorname{Re}$; hence $n\times E_{\rm tot}=n\times E_{\rm tot,tang}=0$ on $\partial O\times\mathbb R$ by [F7]. This is (b). [step 3.1, F2, F7, algebra]

By linearity [F6] the total tangential trace is $\widetilde E_{\rm inc,tang}+\widetilde E''_{\rm tang}$, so the vanishing of the total trace is equivalent to $\widetilde E''_{\rm tang}=e_T$; by step 2.2 applied to $(\widetilde E'',\widetilde B'')$, the correction equals $(\widetilde E_{\rm scat},\widetilde B_{\rm scat})$ on $D$, hence the total equals $(\widetilde E_{\rm tot},\widetilde B_{\rm tot})$; conversely the constructed total has these properties by steps 3.1, 4.2 and the outgoing property of $\widetilde E_{\rm scat}$ from step 1.1. This is the equivalent formulation of (c). [step 3.1, step 4.2, step 2.2, F6, algebra]

Assume the declared normal orientation conditions $k_i\cdot n\in\mathbb R_{>0}$ and $k_r\cdot n\in\mathbb R_{<0}$; no order is placed on a complex number. Tangential components may be complex. No outgoing or non-growth condition is required here. A consuming Fresnel construction may optionally select a root $k_t\cdot n$ of $(k_t\cdot n)^2=\varepsilon_2\mu_2\omega_t^2-\kappa_t\cdot\kappa_t$, where $\kappa_t:=k_t-(k_t\cdot n)n$, with $\operatorname{Im}(k_t\cdot n)\ge0$ and $\operatorname{Re}(k_t\cdot n)\ge0$ when its imaginary part is zero. Define the wave fields $E_j(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(e_j e^{i(k_j\cdot x-\omega_jt)}\bigr)$, $H_j(x,t):=\operatorname{Re}\bigl(h_j e^{i(k_j\cdot x-\omega_jt)}\bigr)$, which are fields of [[def-em-fields]], and let $E:=E_i+E_r$, $H:=H_i+H_r$ on the medium-1 side and $E:=E_t$, $H:=H_t$ on the medium-2 side. $$n\cdot\bigl(\varepsilon_2E_t-\varepsilon_1(E_i+E_r)\bigr)=0,\qquad n\cdot\bigl(\mu_2H_t-\mu_1(H_i+H_r)\bigr)=0,$$
$$n\times\bigl(E_t-(E_i+E_r)\bigr)=0,\qquad n\times\bigl(H_t-(H_i+H_r)\bigr)=0 .$$

$$U_q(\delta,R):=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\{\delta\le|x-x_0|\le R\}}|E_q(x)|^2\,d\lambda_3(x)$$
(the truncated field energy of the shell between the two spheres, [[def-metric-ball]]).
Then:

(c) [Limits of the mass inference] the identity is a divergence of the *field energy of the idealised point source* in the framework's SI conventions. It does not assert that a physical particle has infinite rest mass, does not identify field energy with rest mass, contains no measurement, and involves neither a self-force nor a contradiction claim for classical electrodynamics: the framework supplies no mass-energy identification for a charged particle, and the smooth compact-source field/assembly energy of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] remains finite. Define the retarded potentials by the explicit retarded integrals

$$\varphi(x,t):=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\rho\bigl(y,t-|x-y|/c\bigr)}{|x-y|}\,dy,\qquad A(x,t):=\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{J\bigl(y,t-|x-y|/c\bigr)}{|x-y|}\,dy,$$

and put $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\nabla\times A$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]). Then:

(a) [Smoothness and wave equations] $\varphi$ and each component of $A$ are of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, and $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $WA=\mu_0J$ pointwise.

(b) [Lorenz gauge] With $G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi$ one has $G=0$ on $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$: the retarded pair is in Lorenz gauge, and this is exactly where the continuity hypothesis is used.

(c) [Maxwell fields] $E$ and $B$ are of class $C^\infty$ and the tuple $(E,B,\rho,J)$ satisfies the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the whole of $\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$: $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\nabla\times E=-\partial_tB$, $\nabla\times B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$.

(d) [No field before the source] $E=B=0$ at every event with $t<t_0$ (indeed $\varphi=A=0$ there): the selected retarded solution carries no field from before the source acted.

(e) [Zero-data Cauchy identification] For every $t_1<t_0$ the pair $(\varphi,A)$ restricted to $\mathbb R^3\times[t_1,\infty)$ is the unique $C^2$ extension solution of the wave Cauchy problem of [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] at time $t_1$ with zero Cauchy data and sources $\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\mu_0J$.

(f) [Total charge] The total charge $Q(t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\rho(y,t)\,dy$ is zero for every $t$: a source that is smooth, compactly supported in space and restricted to a compact time interval and satisfies continuity carries zero total charge, so this branch does not model an eternal isolated nonzero charge.

(g) [Scope] This is the compact smooth branch with an adopted causal selection; it asserts nothing about point, line or sheet sources, about weak or distributional branches, about finite-energy or decay properties, about radiation reaction or self-force, and no empirical claim. (a) [Rectangular cavity] In the exact zero-normal-$B$ reflection-parity and divergence class of [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] and [[def-em-guide-cavity-geometry]](c), every initial pair has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ distributional solution of this damped system in the same class. The Fourier coefficient equations at $k_j=\pi n_j/L_j$ are $\widehat E_t=iv^2 k\times\widehat B-\gamma\widehat E$, $\widehat B_t=-ik\times\widehat E$, with both transverse constraints and the original parities retained.
(b) [Smooth closed PEC cavity] Assume the full Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) inherited from the smooth spectral and elliptic suppliers. On a bounded smooth cavity $\Omega$, let $X,V,H$ and its smooth orthonormal eigenfields $u_j$, $\lambda_j\ge0$, be exactly [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]] and [[thm-em-waveguide-spectral-completeness]]. Define the full weak normal-zero divergence-free magnetic space $$M:=\{B\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\int_\Omega B\cdot\nabla\psi=0\text{ for every smooth scalar }\psi\text{ on }\overline\Omega\}.$$ This is the distributional divergence constraint together with weak zero normal flux; for smooth fields it is $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $n\cdot B=0$. For every positive eigenvalue put $w_j=\operatorname{curl}u_j/\sqrt{\lambda_j}$ and put $K_M=\{B\in M:\operatorname{curl}B=0\text{ distributionally}\}$. Then $$M=\overline{\operatorname{span}\{w_j:\lambda_j>0\}}^{L^2}\mathbin{\oplus}K_M.$$ The declared first-order PEC modal energy class is $H\times M$, with weak modal equations $a_j'=v^2\sqrt{\lambda_j}b_j-\gamma a_j$, $b_j'=-\sqrt{\lambda_j}a_j$ for positive modes, $a_j'=-\gamma a_j$ for electric zero modes, and $(B,K_M)'=0$ for every kernel test. Define $D_M$ as the graph-norm completion of finite $w_j$ sums plus $K_M$, with norm squared $\|w\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{curl}w\|_2^2$. The equivalent weak-in-time variational equations are $\langle E_t,\phi\rangle=v^2\langle B,\operatorname{curl}\phi\rangle-\gamma\langle E,\phi\rangle$ for $\phi\in V$, and $\langle B_t,\psi\rangle=-\langle E,\operatorname{curl}\psi\rangle$ for $\psi\in D_M$. They use the actual electric tangential-zero domain $V$ and magnetic normal-zero space $M$, with no claim of maximal-trace equality. For every initial pair in $H\times M$ there is a unique $C(\mathbb R;H\times M)$ solution of that declared realization, which also satisfies the displayed evolution equations distributionally in the interior. Finite electric and paired-magnetic modal sums, with the exact static magnetic kernel component retained, converge uniformly on compact time intervals in energy norm. No equality with every maximal rough tangential-trace realization is asserted.
(c) [Exact energy balance, decay and zero sectors] In both declared classes, for every $t_0<t_1$, $$\mathcal U(t_1)+\sigma\int_{t_0}^{t_1}\|E(t)\|_2^2\,dt=\mathcal U(t_0),\qquad \mathcal U'(t)=-\sigma\|E(t)\|_2^2\le0.$$ For positive smooth-cavity modes $a_j''+\gamma a_j'+v^2\lambda_ja_j=0$. The full Choice premise belongs to the smooth-cavity spectral realization, not to these finite root formulas. For $\sigma>0$ every positive mode decays, electric zero modes obey $a_j(t)=a_j(0)e^{-\gamma t}$, and magnetic kernel data stay constant. This broader wave is retained alongside the physical first-order branch. All square roots and real derivatives use [[thm-of-square-roots]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and the real-component exponential formula [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]].

Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) suffices for the rectangular/Fourier branch; the smooth branch retains its actual full Choice premise. Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the convention of
the test-geometry and divergence-theorem items cited below
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory
region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of
[[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ fields of
[[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ source fields of
[[def-em-sources]] satisfying the smooth branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on a neighbourhood of the data below.

Suppose given two patch test geometries $(D,r_1)$, $(D,r_2)$ of
[[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]] over the same finite elementary Green region
$D$ whose induced boundary chains coincide as oriented paths (so both patches
span the same closed loop $\gamma$), and suppose there is a bounded open
region $V\subseteq\Omega$ with a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation
whose boundary faces are exactly the two images $r_1[D]$, $r_2[D]$ with
outward normals $-n_1$ and $+n_2$ respectively, where $n_i$ is the normal
induced by $r_i$ (that is, $V$ is the region enclosed between the two patches;
this is a hypothesis on the pair, part of its data). Then, for every $t\in I$:

(a) [Total current flux is surface independent]

$$\int_{S_1}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS=\int_{S_2}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\oint_\gamma B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r,$$

where $S_i=r_i[D]$ and the flux is that of
[[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]].

(b) [Conduction-only flux need not be] For every $t\in I$ the difference of
the conduction fluxes equals the negative of the difference of the
displacement fluxes:

$$\int_{S_1}J(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS-\int_{S_2}J(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS=-\varepsilon_0\left(\int_{S_1}\partial_tE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS-\int_{S_2}\partial_tE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS\right).$$

Hence the conduction-only fluxes are equal exactly when the displacement
fluxes are equal, and neither conclusion is forced by the Maxwell equations
alone.

(c) [Explicit realisation] The following declared smooth data satisfies all
the hypotheses above and has different conduction fluxes through the two
surfaces. On $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$, fix $\chi\in C^\infty(\mathbb
R)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$, $\chi(z)=1$ for $z\le-1$ and $\chi(z)=0$ for
$z\ge0$, and set

$$E(x,t):=\frac{t}{\varepsilon_0}\chi(z)\,e_z,\qquad B:=0,\qquad \rho(x,t):=t\,\chi'(z),\qquad J(x,t):=-\chi(z)\,e_z.$$

Then $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$,
$\operatorname{curl}E=0=-\partial_tB$,
$\operatorname{curl}B=0=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ (the last identity because
$c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}=\mu_0$), and $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$.
Take $D=[-1,1]^2$ and its interior $D^\circ=(-1,1)^2$. Let $\sigma$ be the
standard smooth step of [[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]] and define
$h(s):=\sigma(2(1-s^2))$, $\eta(u,v):=h(u)h(v)$. Then
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$, $0\le\eta\le1$, $\eta=1$ in a
neighbourhood of the origin, $\eta>0$ at every point of $D^\circ$, and $\eta=0$
on $\partial D$ and outside $D$. Take the graphs

$$r_1(u,v):=(u,v,-2\eta(u,v)),\qquad r_2(u,v):=(u,v,0).$$

Both induced boundary chains are the square
$\{(u,v,0):(u,v)\in\partial D\}$, the region
$V=\{(u,v,w):(u,v)\in D^\circ,\ -2\eta(u,v)<w<0\}$ is enclosed between the
patches, and

$$\int_{S_1}J\cdot n_1\,dS=-\int_D\chi(-2\eta(u,v))\,dudv<0,\qquad \int_{S_2}J\cdot n_2\,dS=-\int_D\chi(0)\,dudv=0,$$

the first inequality because $\eta=1$ in a neighbourhood of the origin, so
$\chi(-2\eta)=1$ on a nonempty open subset of $D$, whose area is positive,
while both total current fluxes in (a) vanish, consistently with the loop
integral $\oint_\gamma B\cdot d\mathbf r=0$. In the standard
charging-capacitor discussion the two spanning surfaces cut the conduction
current in different ways and the difference is carried by the displacement
term; the realisation above exhibits exactly this phenomenon in a
self-contained smooth model. An idealised thin-wire current is not a source
type of this framework and the capacitor interpretation is explanatory, not
an additional empirical claim.
